Your fury answers every miss. When a melee attack misses you and the attacker is within your reach, you may make an attack of opportunity against them. This uses and is limited by your normal attacks of opportunity per round.
Prerequisites: Dex 13, Combat Reflexes.

The surge of your most potent magic carries into your defenses. Whenever you cast a spell using one of your highest-level spell slots, you gain a +1 dodge bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.
Prerequisites: Caster level 3rd.
The cast of a powerful spell leaves a ward of force shimmering around this character, granting a +1 dodge bonus to AC.

Precision comes cheap when the target stops moving. When you reduce an enemy to 0 hit points with a ranged weapon attack, your next ranged attack within 1 round gains a +2 bonus on the attack roll.
Prerequisites: Dex 13, Point-Blank Shot.
Riding the momentum of a kill, this character's next ranged attack gains a +2 bonus on the attack roll.

Once per day, when a hit brings you to half your maximum hit points or below, you catch a second wind: you gain temporary hit points equal to your character level (minimum 2) and a +2 morale bonus on Fortitude saves for 1 minute. The daily use is restored when you rest.
Prerequisites: Endurance.
Gritting through the pain, this character gains temporary hit points equal to their character level and a +2 morale bonus on Fortitude saves.

Your brutal swings do more than wound. When you hit with a melee attack while Power Attack is active, the target suffers a -2 penalty on attack rolls for 1 round as pain and fury cloud its focus. A new hit refreshes the duration.
Prerequisites: Str 13, Power Attack.
Staggered by a vicious blow, this creature takes a -2 penalty on attack rolls.

When you confirm a critical hit with an unarmed strike, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half your character level + Wisdom modifier) or take a -2 penalty to AC for 1 round. The penalty cannot be applied again while it is already active. Prerequisites: Wis 13, Improved Unarmed Strike.
Harmonic vibrations from an unarmed critical strike rattle this creature's defenses, imposing a -2 penalty to AC.

You were born under the wardstones of Kenabres, and their echo lingers in your blood. You gain a +1 luck bonus on Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saving throws.
Prerequisites: Iron Will.

A test harness for the Mission WOTR mod: this archetype grants all seven Mission WOTR feats at level 1, along with the vanilla feats they normally require, so their mechanics can be exercised from the first fight. It removes nothing from the standard Magus kit. Intended to be expanded into a full class in a future version.

You move with impossible grace, twisting through the air like a leaf on the wind. You gain an additional +4 bonus on Mobility and Athletics checks.
Adapted from the tabletop mythic feat; Wrath folds Acrobatics and Fly into Mobility and Athletics.

Your words bend wills like reeds in a storm, and no lie slips past you. You gain an additional +4 bonus on Persuasion checks and an additional +4 bonus on Perception checks.
Prerequisites: Persuasive.
Adapted from the tabletop mythic feat; Wrath folds Sense Motive into Persuasion and Perception.

Magic answers your touch like an old friend. You gain an additional +4 bonus on Knowledge (Arcana) and Use Magic Device checks.
Adapted from the tabletop mythic feat.

Death feeds your legend. Whenever you reduce an enemy to 0 hit points with a weapon attack, you gain temporary hit points equal to your mythic rank (minimum 2) for 1 minute. This cannot be gained again while active.
Legends are written in blood. The character's latest kill invigorates them, granting temporary hit points.

Your spells leave a wake of power that sharpens your strikes. Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher from one of your spellbooks, you gain a +1 insight bonus on attack rolls for 1 round, increasing by +1 for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +1). This cannot be gained again while active.
The residue of a recent spell hones this character's aim, granting an insight bonus on attack rolls.

Your mind is a fortress no mortal power may breach. You gain a +1 insight bonus on Will saving throws for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +2).
Prerequisites: Iron Will.

You react to danger before it finishes arriving. You gain a +1 insight bonus on Reflex saving throws for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +2).
Prerequisites: Lightning Reflexes.

Your body endures what should destroy it. You gain a +1 insight bonus on Fortitude saving throws for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +2).
Prerequisites: Endurance.
Blades pass through the spaces you occupied a heartbeat ago. You gain a +1 dodge bonus to AC for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +1).
Wounds focus the legend within. While you are at or below half your hit points, you gain a +1 dodge bonus to AC for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +1).
Nothing sharpens the mind like mortality. While you are at or below half your hit points, you gain a +1 insight bonus on attack rolls for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +1).

Every assault you shrug off stokes the legend. Whenever you succeed at a saving throw against an effect created by another creature, you gain a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls for 1 round per 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +2). This cannot be gained again while active.
Having just shrugged off an enemy effect, this character fights with renewed conviction, gaining a morale bonus on attack rolls.

A kill today is momentum for the next. Whenever you reduce an enemy to 0 hit points with a weapon attack, you gain a +1 insight bonus on attack rolls for 1 round per 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +2). This cannot be gained again while active.
Fresh from a kill, this character's next blows strike with terrifying precision, gaining an insight bonus on attack rolls.

Magic leaves a shield in its wake. Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher from one of your spellbooks, you gain a +1 deflection bonus to AC for 1 round per 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +1). This cannot be gained again while active.
The residue of a recently cast spell forms a protective shell around this character, granting a deflection bonus to AC.
The strength of legend flows through every blow. You gain a +1 mythic bonus on weapon damage rolls for every mythic rank you possess.
Your flesh hardens like living stone. You gain a +1 natural armor bonus to AC for every 2 mythic ranks you possess (minimum +1).

Pick your moment when steel is already crossed. You gain a +1 bonus on ranged attack rolls against enemies engaged in melee with one of your allies.
Prerequisites: Dex 13, Point-Blank Shot.

Each blow that fails to find you hardens your guard. Each time a melee attack misses you, you gain a +1 dodge bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, stacking up to +3.
Prerequisites: Combat Expertise.
Turning aside successive blows, this character's guard grows harder to breach, granting a dodge bonus to AC.

You hold ground like a cornered beast. While this stance is active, you may make any number of attacks of opportunity each round, but you take a -2 penalty on all attack rolls.
Prerequisites: Combat Reflexes.
Fighting with the desperate precision of a cornered beast, this character makes any number of attacks of opportunity but suffers a penalty on attack rolls.

An eldritch poisoner blends volatile chemicals with her own magic to create arcanotoxins. A number of times per day equal to her alchemist level + Intelligence modifier, she can brew a dose and coat a weapon with it; hits then require a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half alchemist level + Intelligence) or 1d2 Strength damage. Arcanotoxin is supernatural and bypasses poison immunity, though such creatures gain +4 on the save. This replaces bomb, Throw Anything, and mutagen, and grants sneak attack as a rogue. Ported from Pathfinder Player Companion: Black Markets.

A number of times per day equal to her alchemist level + Intelligence modifier, she can brew a dose of arcanotoxin and coat a weapon with it for 1 minute. Hits with the coated weapon require a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half alchemist level + Intelligence modifier) or 1d2 Strength damage for 2 rounds. A creature cannot be affected by a new dose while one is active. Arcanotoxin is supernatural and affects creatures immune to poison, though they gain +4 on the save.
Brew a dose of arcanotoxin (expending one daily use) and coat your weapon with it for 1 minute. Standard action.

Brew and apply a dose of arcanotoxin as a swift action - at a price. You lose 25% of your maximum hit points, or only 15% if you succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save. This can never reduce you below 1 hit point.
A sheen of supernatural poison coats this character's weapon. Hits with the weapon deliver the arcanotoxin.
A supernatural poison courses through this character's veins, weakening its muscles.
You are trained in the creation of poisons and antitoxins. You gain a +2 bonus on Lore (Nature) checks related to alchemy and toxins.

You may brew and apply a dose of arcanotoxin as a swift action instead of a standard action. The accelerated reaction burns you: you lose 25% of your maximum hit points, or only 15% if you succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save. This can never reduce you below 1 hit point.

Your arcanotoxin leaves victims retching. When a creature fails its saving throw against your arcanotoxin, it is also sickened for the toxin's duration. Beginning at 12th level, targets are nauseated instead.

Your arcanotoxin induces vivid hallucinations. When a creature fails its saving throw against your arcanotoxin, it is also dazzled for the toxin's duration. Beginning at 10th level, targets are confused instead.
Prerequisites: Eldritch Poisoner, alchemist level 6.

Your arcanotoxin locks muscles rigid. When a creature fails its saving throw against your arcanotoxin, it is also staggered for the toxin's duration. Beginning at 15th level, targets are paralyzed instead.
Prerequisites: Eldritch Poisoner, alchemist level 8.

Your arcanotoxin attacks life itself. Your arcanotoxin deals Constitution damage instead of Strength damage.
Prerequisites: Eldritch Poisoner, alchemist level 10.
You diversify your arcanotoxin, striking both muscle and reflex. Your arcanotoxin deals 1 point of Strength damage and 1 point of Dexterity damage instead of its normal damage.

You can create your arcanotoxin as a contact poison, delivered by a hurled vial. You may throw a vial of arcanotoxin at an enemy within 30 feet as a standard action; on contact it delivers your arcanotoxin at a save DC 2 lower than normal.
Prerequisites: Eldritch Poisoner, alchemist level 4.
Hurl a vial of contact arcanotoxin at an enemy, expending one daily use. On contact it delivers her arcanotoxin with a save DC 2 lower than normal.

You can create your arcanotoxin as an inhaled poison. You may throw a vial of arcanotoxin that bursts in a 10-foot cloud (expending one daily use); enemies in the area are subjected to your arcanotoxin with a save DC 4 lower than normal.
Prerequisites: Eldritch Poisoner, alchemist level 6.
Hurl a vial of arcanotoxin that bursts into a 10-foot cloud of fumes, expending one daily use. Enemies in the area are subjected to her arcanotoxin with a save DC 4 lower than normal.
You can create and apply your arcanotoxin to a held weapon - your own or an ally's - as a move action. The toxin lasts 1 minute or until used.
Brew a dose of arcanotoxin (expending one daily use) and coat the target's weapon with it for 1 minute. Move action.
You can sacrifice one use of your arcanotoxin to create an extract of delay poison, which you can feed to an adjacent willing creature as a standard action.
Sacrifice one use of arcanotoxin to shield an ally from poison for 1 minute, as delay poison.
You know venoms the way a scholar knows books. You gain a bonus on Lore (Nature) checks equal to half your alchemist level.
You know precisely where a blade carries poison best. When you deliver your arcanotoxin with a sneak attack, the saving throw DC increases by 2.

A metallics-themed engineer who deploys construct summons: uncontrollable, relentless, and deliberately less customizable than a companion. One construct of each base may be active at a time; deploying the same base again replaces the old one. Bases: Iron-Hearted Hound at 1st level, Humanoid Construct at 7th, Stone Golem at 16th. Cores and programs are chosen before deployment. This replaces mutagen and the alchemist's poison features, and grants an extra combat feat at 1st level.

Deploy an iron-hearted hound - a dog whose iron heart makes it immune to fear and mind control (standard action). Its plating grants damage reduction equal to half your alchemist level, bypassed by adamantine. The hound acts on its own - it cannot be controlled - and remains until destroyed or until you deploy another hound.

Deploy a humanoid construct (standard action): a fighter with fighter levels equal to your alchemist level minus 2, equipped with simple arms and armor. It acts on its own and remains until destroyed or replaced.

Deploy a stone golem (standard action): a hulking construct without its kind's berserk tendency and somewhat weaker than the standard golem. It acts on its own and remains until destroyed or replaced.
The basic core: each base deploys with its standard chassis - the hound's plating, the humanoid's fighter training, and the golem's bulk. Future cores will offer different stat packages.
The basic program: the construct charges the nearest enemy and attacks until it or the enemy is destroyed. Future programs will offer other behaviors.
Choose the core that powers the crafter's constructs. The core determines their stat package.
Choose the program that directs the crafter's constructs. The program determines their behavior.
Masterwork plating grants this construct damage reduction equal to half its crafter's alchemist level, bypassed by adamantine weapons.
The crafter is trained with light armor, longbows, shortbows, throwing axes, flails, heavy flails, warhammers, greatclubs, and simple weapons.
The crafter's extract formulae are deliberately hasty imitations. Caster level for alchemist extracts is reduced by one step per two alchemist levels, to roughly half level.

The construct stays out of harm's way. While this program is active, deployed constructs take a penalty on attack rolls and initiative equal to half your alchemist level, but gain a dodge bonus to AC and a bonus on all saving throws of the same amount.

The construct pursues destruction single-mindedly. While this program is active, deployed constructs gain a bonus on attack rolls and initiative equal to half your alchemist level, but take an equal penalty to AC and a -2 penalty on all saving throws.

While this program is active, deployed constructs gain sneak attack dice equal to half your alchemist level, applying to any attack roll including spell rays. Their base attack bonus is reduced by half your alchemist level, and every ability they use resolves at a caster level penalty equal to your full alchemist level.

The construct interposes itself. While this program is active, deployed constructs gain a dodge bonus to AC and additional attacks of opportunity equal to half your alchemist level, but deal damage reduced by your full alchemist level.

The construct keeps its distance. While this program is active, deployed constructs gain a base attack bonus equal to half your alchemist level, but take an equal penalty to AC, a -2 penalty on attack rolls, and a -2 penalty on all saving throws.

The construct's logic is blessed - or cursed - by the Abyss. While this program is active, deployed constructs gain a bonus to attack rolls, AC, initiative, and all saving throws equal to half your alchemist level. However, while a chaos construct of a given base lives, you cannot deploy another construct of that base.
This construct runs on chaos logic. While it lives, its crafter cannot deploy another construct of the same base.

Redline the construct. While this core is active, deployed constructs gain a bonus on attack rolls and damage equal to half your alchemist level and +10 foot speed, but take 2 damage each round and cannot be healed. The Overdrive core cannot be combined with the Chaos program.

Fortify the chassis. While this core is active, deployed constructs gain a dodge bonus to AC and a bonus on all saving throws equal to half your alchemist level, and damage reduction 2, but their damage is reduced by the same amount.

Bind an elemental fire. Iron-Hearted Hound: +10 foot speed, bonus damage and saves equal to half alchemist level, and sneak attack, but reduced AC and 1 damage each round. Humanoid Construct: attacks deal +2d6 fire damage and set enemies burning. Stone Golem: wreathed in flame that scorches nearby enemies and ignites those it strikes, but it makes no attacks of opportunity (the Guard program restores them) and burns for 2 damage each round.

Bind an elemental rime. Iron-Hearted Hound: hits knock enemies prone and slow them; +saves (half alchemist level), -10 foot speed. Humanoid Construct: +20 foot speed and +damage (half alchemist level) - it charges like a skater on black ice. Stone Golem: attacks deal +1d6 cold damage and slow enemies.
A sanguine engine. While this core is active, deployed constructs make enemies bleed and shake on every hit, and the construct mends itself with fast healing 2.

A yielding, sponge-like chassis. While this core is active, deployed constructs gain a dodge bonus to AC and a bonus on all saves equal to half your alchemist level, and fast healing 1, at the cost of reduced damage. It keeps enemies busy while your party works.
A sliver of Hell. While this core is active, deployed constructs deal +2d6 fire damage, shake enemies they strike, and gain +10 foot speed and initiative (half alchemist level).

A heart of pure shadow. Iron-Hearted Hound and Humanoid Construct: sneak attack (1 die per 3 alchemist levels) plus attack and dodge bonuses (half alchemist level). Stone Golem: strikes shake and frighten enemies, and it gains will save bonuses.

An unstable resonator. While this core is active, deployed constructs deal greatly increased damage and every weapon hit detonates in a concussive blast dealing sonic damage to enemies near the target, but the construct suffers reduced AC and -2 on all saving throws. The blast starts at 1d6 and grows by one die per 5 alchemist levels, up to 5d6.

Lightweight servos everywhere. While this core is active, deployed constructs gain an extra attack each round (as haste), +10 foot speed, and initiative bonuses (half alchemist level), at the cost of some damage.
A storm in a bottle. While this core is active, deployed constructs deal +1d6 electricity damage on hit and gain bonuses to initiative and Reflex saves (half your alchemist level) and +10 foot speed.

A living lodestone. While this core is active, deployed constructs gain bonuses to combat maneuvers and their defense against them (half your alchemist level), and enemies they strike are slowed as metal drags at their limbs.
This construct's chassis cannot make attacks of opportunity.
This unit was deployed by a Construct Crafter (hound base).
This unit was deployed by a Construct Crafter (humanoid base).
This unit was deployed by a Construct Crafter (golem base).
The construct vent its core: a 15-foot burst of flame deals 6d6 fire damage (Reflex half).
A freezing ray deals 4d6 cold damage (Reflex half) and slows the target for 3 rounds.
Hasty patchwork grants this unit temporary hit points from its crafter's alchemist level.
Patch an ally's plating: the target gains temporary hit points equal to the crafter's alchemist level (minimum 5) for 1 minute.
The construct launches a shard of metal: 2d6 piercing damage (Reflex half).

A mounted ballista assembly. While this core is active, deployed constructs gain a bonus on attack rolls and damage equal to half your alchemist level and +10 foot speed, but suffer an equal penalty to AC. The humanoid construct fields a longbow; the hound and golem spit bolts from range.

The construct tears a hole in space and appears beside its prey, striking with its weapon. This is a teleporting attack: the construct moves next to the target and makes a full weapon attack (attack roll, critical hits, and sneak attack all apply). Usable once per round.
The crafter's constructs are bound to their maker and follow them.

You fight whatever the enemy is hiding behind. Destructive lends half your barbarian level as bonus damage on weapon attacks against constructs, Battle Scavenger grants growing expertise with clubs, staves, and spears, and Sunder Armor is a combat maneuver that dents a target's protection. (Tabletop port: unattended objects and improvised weapons have no Wrath equivalent.)
A standard action against one enemy within reach. Roll a combat maneuver check against the target's CMD; on a success its armor is damaged and the protection it provides is reduced.
Whenever you hit a construct with a weapon attack, you deal bonus damage equal to half your barbarian level (minimum +1). This replaces fast movement.

You know how to make junk kill. You gain +1 bonus damage with scavenged arms (clubs, greatclubs, quarterstaves, spears, daggers, sickles, maces, flails) for every three barbarian levels beyond 3rd. (The tabletop version works with improvised and broken weapons, which do not exist in Wrath.)

While raging your weapon attacks open bleeding wounds that stack five deep, you heal faster for every bleeding enemy nearby, and critical hits against bleeding foes spray gore and terror across their neighbors. Open the Floodgate spends every bleed stack around you in a single surge of self-healing. This replaces uncanny dodge, improved uncanny dodge, and damage reduction.

While raging: your weapon attacks apply a Bleeding Wound (1d4 bleed per round, stacking up to five times per target); and you gain fast healing 1 while at least one enemy within 30 feet is bleeding (2 at three or more, 3 at five or more). Any source of bleed counts. This replaces uncanny dodge.
A wound opened by a Bloodstorm's rage. Deals 1d4 damage per round for each stack, until the Bloodstorm opens the floodgate or the victim dies.

While raging, when you score a critical hit against a bleeding target, blood sprays: every enemy within 10 feet of the target gains a Bleeding Wound and is shaken for 1 round. This replaces improved uncanny dodge.

While raging, you can open your wounds and drink the storm: every Bleeding Wound on enemies within 30 feet is consumed, and you heal 1d6 damage per stack consumed. This replaces your damage reduction.

The covert mage treats her magic as one more con. Persuasion, Perception, Stealth, and Thievery become class skills; she casts in light armor without penalty; her touch softens a mind; her spell tricks provoke nothing from a target she has feinted; and she sees through illusions. This replaces the arcanist exploits gained at 3rd, 7th, and 11th level.

A covert mage adds Persuasion, Perception, Stealth and Thievery to her class skills, and gains proficiency with light armor. She can cast arcanist spells while wearing light armor without incurring arcane spell failure (heavier armor still applies its full spell failure chance).

As a standard action, the covert mage can spend 1 point from her arcane reservoir to make a melee touch attack. If it hits, the target takes a penalty on Will saves equal to the covert mage's arcanist level for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
The target takes a penalty on Will saves equal to the covert mage's arcanist level.

When she casts a spell with a casting time of 1 standard action that targets a creature she is adjacent to, she may feint as part of the casting: a Persuasion check against 10 + the target's Hit Dice + its Wisdom modifier. On a success the spell does not provoke an attack of opportunity from that target, and the target rolls its saving throw twice and takes the lesser result.

The covert mage has become an expert at seeing through others' illusions because of her own mastery at weaving them. Her saving throws against illusion effects are rolled twice and she takes the better result.
Feinted by a covert mage: the target cannot make attacks of opportunity for 1 round.

The elemental obsessor forsakes every spell that is not of her chosen element and claims the rest of the world's arsenal for her own book. Her focus adds force to every cast, her obsession makes resistances and immunities leak, her kills erupt, and every death by her element refills her arcane reservoir. This replaces the arcanist exploits gained at 1st, 3rd, and 7th level.

Choose one element: Fire, Cold, Acid, Electricity or Sonic. The arcanist spellbook is replaced - the obsessor can only prepare and cast spells that carry her element's descriptor, but the list is drawn from every non-mythic spellbook in the game, each spell at its lowest level anywhere. Every spell in the book casts with Intelligence, whatever its origin.

Your fixation is FIRE. You can only learn, prepare and cast spells of the fire descriptor - but every fire spell from every non-mythic spellbook in the game is on your list. Fire perk: Cathartic Release erupts with one extra damage die.

Your fixation is COLD. You can only learn, prepare and cast spells of the cold descriptor - but every cold spell from every non-mythic spellbook in the game is on your list. Cold perk: Cathartic Release erupts with one extra damage die.

Your fixation is ACID. You can only learn, prepare and cast spells of the acid descriptor - but every acid spell from every non-mythic spellbook in the game is on your list. Acid perk: Corrosive Adaptation - at 12th, 16th and 20th level you may adopt a spell from another element's list; it becomes an acid spell for you.

Your fixation is ELECTRICITY. You can only learn, prepare and cast spells of the electricity descriptor - but every electricity spell from every non-mythic spellbook in the game is on your list. Electricity perk: Unstoppable Obsession floors damage at 40% instead of 20%, rising to the same 105% at 20th level.

Your fixation is SONIC. You can only learn, prepare and cast spells of the sonic descriptor - every sonic spell from every non-mythic spellbook in the game is on your list. Sonic perk: Shattering Pitch - your single-target sonic spells splash 25% of their damage to enemies within 10 feet.

Her magic is honed to a razor's edge. Whenever she casts a damaging spell, one hit of that cast - the first ray, or the first tick of a persistent effect - deals additional damage equal to half her arcanist level, minimum 1. Cantrips receive half this bonus, minimum 1.

When her chosen element's damage is reduced by immunity or resistance, the target still takes at least 20% of the raw damage, and the floor rises by 5% for every arcanist level beyond 3rd. At 20th level the target takes 105% of the raw damage, as if it were weak to her element. Electricity obsessors begin at 40%; the cap is the same.

When a single-target spell of yours kills an enemy, the pent-up element erupts: every other enemy within 10 feet of the victim takes 1d4 points of damage per two arcanist levels beyond 7th (1d4 at 7th, up to 7d4 at 19th; 8d4 for fire and cold obsessors).

The hunt feeds the obsession. Whenever a spell of her chosen element kills an enemy, she regains 1 point of arcane reservoir, never exceeding her maximum - the same reservoir that powers her arcane exploits and Consume Spells.
Her sonic spells strike a frequency that shatters. When a single-target sonic spell of hers damages an enemy, every other enemy within 10 feet of it takes 25% of the damage dealt.

Her acid digests even magic that was never acid to begin with. Choose a spell from another element's list: it is added to her acid spell list, and whenever she casts it its damage is converted to acid. She may choose again at 16th and 20th level.

The mummer mage performs for prestige rather than applause, and she is very good at pretending. Shtick of the Magi replaces bardic knowledge; Imperious Gestures replaces well-versed; Arcane Imitation replaces inspire competence; Method Acting replaces lore master; and Eucatastrophe replaces jack-of-all-trades.

The mummer mage begins with an ornate masterwork quarterstaff that serves as a masterwork prop, granting a +2 circumstance bonus on Persuasion checks to convince others of her arcane mastery. If it is ever lost, she can replace it for 400 gp. This replaces bardic knowledge.
Starting at 2nd level, the mummer mage gains a +2 bonus on concentration checks when casting bard spells (WOTR simplification: all her casting). This replaces well-versed.

She selects one spell from the wizard spell list of a level she can cast and adds it to her bard spells known, gaining an additional pick at 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, and again at 16th and 19th. This replaces versatile performance, which does not exist in Wrath, so the feature is additive.

Starting at 5th level, the shtick of the magi grants the mummer mage all the benefits of a bonded item, as the wizard's arcane bond class feature: once per day she may cast any one spell from her spellbook through the prop as a full-round action.

At 5th level, the mummer mage so thoroughly maintains her wizardly persona that knowledge comes easy: she uses her Charisma instead of Intelligence on all Knowledge (Lore) skill checks - she remembers playing a scholar, convincingly. This replaces lore master.

At 10th level she gains an additional Arcane Imitation pick, a wizard spell of a level she can cast, and again at 16th and 19th - three extra spells beyond her regular imitation. Together with the bonded prop's daily cast, any bard spell she knows is one flourish away. This replaces jack-of-all-trades.

The Cook trades every performance, all bardic knowledge, dirge of doom, jack-of-all-trades, and mass suggestion for a fire, a knife, and three good meals a day. Hearty Cooking grants 3 meal charges per rest; each serving feeds every ally within 30 feet a meal whose benefits last 8 hours and cannot be dispelled. A new recipe arrives at 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

The cook prepares 3 meals per long rest. Each Serve ability spends one meal charge and feeds every ally within 30 feet: the meal's buff lasts 8 hours, scales with her bard level, and cannot be dispelled.
The cook's repertoire grows. She learns one new meal: Garlic, Chili Pepper, Cheese, Mushroom, Potato, Onion, Coffee, or Butter.
Barded meat, tender and rich: everyone served gains 1 bonus hit point, plus 1 more for every 4 cook levels.
Lean protein, honest food: everyone served gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls.
A steady staple: everyone served gains a +1 bonus on all saving throws.
Fiber and fuel: everyone served gains 5 feet of movement speed.
Light and crisp: everyone served gains a +1 bonus to AC that grows as the cook levels.
Pungent and persuasive: everyone served gains a +2 bonus on Persuasion checks.
It bites back: everyone served deals 1 bonus damage on attacks.
Aged and cultured: everyone served gains a +2 bonus on all Knowledge (Lore) checks.
Foraged and earthy: everyone served gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks.
Sturdy root vegetable: everyone served gains a +2 bonus on Fortitude saves.
It brings tears and sharpens the senses: everyone served gains a +2 bonus on Perception checks.
Black and bitter: everyone served gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks and 5 feet of movement speed.
Everything is better with it: everyone served gains a +1 bonus on all saving throws.

The spellfist casts with Wisdom from a spellbook of touch spells only, and never lands a spell as a single blow - each casting is divided among the attacks of his full attack. His flurry bypasses armor and damage reduction, his fists grow from 1d6 to 1d8 to 2d6, and he keeps spell combat, spell strike, and his arcane pool. This replaces all weapon and armor proficiencies, granting improved unarmed strike instead.

He never lands a spell as one blow. Casting a touch spell charges his fists for 2 rounds; the spell's damage is divided into one share per attack of his full attack, and each successful unarmed strike delivers one share of the original dice and energy. A cast not followed by unarmed attacks dissipates harmlessly. Non-damaging touch effects apply normally.
A touch spell is held in the Spellfist's fists. Each successful unarmed attack delivers one share of the spell's damage. If the fists do not strike before the charge fades, the spell dissipates.

The Spellfist forgos all weapons and armor. He gains Improved Unarmed Strike and the first of a monk's unarmed damage increases, but no weapon or armor proficiencies - anything he wields swings with non-proficient penalties, and his fists never grow as mighty as a true monk's.

While unarmored and unshielded, the Spellfist adds his Wisdom modifier to his AC, and his fists blur: he gains one extra attack when taking a full attack, at a -2 penalty on all attacks during the flurry.
Extra unarmed attack from the flurry; -2 on attack rolls; Wisdom bonus to AC.

Each of the Spellfist's unarmed hits cracks the target's guard, stacking the Sundered effect: every weapon attack against the target treats its damage reduction as 2 lower per stack (up to a rank cap that grows with level).
This creature's damage reduction is compromised: every weapon attack against it treats its DR as 2 lower per rank of this effect.
The act of casting hardens the Spellfist. While his fists are charged with a spell, he gains damage reduction equal to a quarter of his class level (minimum 1 at 7th).
Casting has hardened the Spellfist's skin: he has damage reduction while this lasts.
Light of foot and light of hand: the Spellfist's base movement speed increases by 5 feet.

A spellblade magus can manifest a ghostly blade of force that can be used as an off-hand weapon.
Force Athame (Sp): At 2nd level, a spellblade magus can sacrifice a prepared magus spell of 1st level or higher as a swift action to create a dagger of force in his off hand. The athame lasts for 1 minute or until dismissed, has an enhancement bonus on attack and damage rolls equal to the level of the spell sacrificed (maximum +5), acts as a dagger, and attacks with it are force attacks that deal force damage. The hand holding it is still considered free for spell combat and delivering touch attacks.
This replaces spellstrike.

As a swift action, sacrifice a prepared magus spell of 1st level or higher to create a dagger of force in his off hand. The athame lasts 1 minute, has an enhancement bonus on attack and damage equal to the sacrificed spell's level (maximum +5), and deals force damage. The off hand remains free for spell combat.

A dagger of force hovers at the spellblade's side, striking as a force dagger with an enhancement bonus equal to the level of the spell sacrificed to create it. It shatters if thrown true or parried with.
The shattered athame's force wraps around the spellblade as a deflection bonus to AC until the end of his next turn.
Instead of sacrificing a prepared spell, the spellblade can spend 3 points from his arcane pool as a swift action to create the force athame with a +3 enhancement bonus.

When an enemy makes a melee attack against the spellblade while his athame is active, the athame shatters into a ward: it ends immediately and grants him a deflection bonus to AC until the end of his next turn equal to the level of the spell sacrificed to create it (maximum +5).
As a standard action, the spellblade can throw his athame as a ranged attack. If it misses, it returns automatically just before his next turn. If it hits, it deals its damage and its duration ends.
As Throw Athame, but the spellblade spends 2 arcane pool points to add +2d6 force damage on a hit.

A bloodrager whose rage closes wounds instead of opening them. While bloodraging she radiates an aura that heals nearby allies at the start of each of her turns, and she can spend rounds of bloodrage for pulses of healing or fast healing. At the height of fury she can spend every remaining round to pull a dying ally back from death. This replaces uncanny dodge, damage reduction, and spellcasting above 3rd level.

While bloodraging she radiates a 10-foot aura of living vitality. At the start of each of her turns, every ally in the aura below maximum hit points regains 1d4 + 1/3 bloodrager level hit points. At 20th level the aura grows to 40 feet; see Sanguine Apotheosis.

As a swift action while bloodraging she may expend 1 additional round of bloodrage to release a wave of restorative energy. All allies within 20 feet, including herself, regain 1d8 + 1/3 bloodrager level hit points. From 8th level the pulse reaches 30 feet and heals 2d8 + bloodrager level + Constitution modifier, and allies healed from below 0 hit points are stabilized. Once per round.

As Bloodletting Pulse, but the Font opens her own veins to sustain the wave: each ally (other than herself) also gains fast healing (2 at 5th, 3 at 11th, 5 at 16th level) for 3 rounds, while the Font suffers an unremovable bleed of the same amount for 3 rounds.
The perfected pulse: a free action, usable any number of times per round (each use still expends a round of bloodrage). Healing and range as per Greater Bloodletting Pulse.
The Font has already released a pulse this round.

The Font learns to share her vitality at the cost of her own blood. Her Bloodletting Pulse (Shared) grants allies fast healing (2 at 5th, 3 at 11th, 5 at 16th level) for 3 rounds, while she bleeds for the same amount for 3 rounds - a bleed that cannot be removed.
The pulse reaches 30 feet, and its healing becomes 2d8 + bloodrager level + Constitution modifier. Creatures healed from below 0 hit points by the pulse are treated as though they had stabilized.
The Font's blood knits the ally's wounds: fast healing each round while this lasts.
The price of shared vitality: the Font bleeds each round while this lasts. This bleed cannot be removed.
The Sanguine Font trains with simple weapons and light armor only.
Choose the element that runs in the Font's blood: it powers her Kinetic Blade and Kinetic Blast.
The Font's blood burns. Her kinetic powers deal fire damage.
The Font's blood runs ice-cold. Her kinetic powers deal cold damage.
The Font's blood crackles. Her kinetic powers deal electricity damage.
The Font's blood corrodes. Her kinetic powers deal acid damage.
The Font's blood resonates with raw force. Her kinetic powers deal force damage.

Toggle: a blade of elemental force fights at the Font's side, functioning as the kinetic knight's blade. Its damage (1d6 + Con, growing by 1d6 per two effective kineticist levels) is of her chosen element. Effective kineticist level = bloodrager level - 2.
A blade of elemental force strikes alongside the Font, dealing her element's damage plus Constitution.

A ranged touch attack of elemental force (Dexterity to hit, Constitution to damage), dealing 1d6 per odd effective kineticist level (bloodrager level - 2) of the Font's chosen element. It has none of a kineticist's infusions or extra effects - that is the price of the power.

While bloodraging her aura grows to 40 feet and heals 2d8 + Constitution + Charisma + 1/8 of her current hit points + bloodrager level at the start of each turn. Bloodletting Pulse becomes a free action usable any number of times per round, each use still costing a round of bloodrage. Once per bloodrage, when an ally in the aura would die, she may expend all her remaining rounds: that ally remains at 1 hit point and is healed for 10d8 + bloodrager level.

The untouchable rager trades all bloodrager spellcasting for Raging Resistance: while bloodraging she gains spell resistance equal to 8 + her bloodrager level, increasing by 1 at 7th, 10th, 13th, and 16th level, to SR 32 at 20th. The ward cannot be lowered while the rage holds. At 14th level, Resistance Control extends it while calm, where she can suppress it at will.

While bloodraging, the untouchable rager gains spell resistance equal to 8 plus her bloodrager level, plus 1 at 7th, 10th, 13th, and 16th level. The resistance cannot be voluntarily lowered while the rage lasts.

At 14th level, the untouchable rager keeps her spell resistance even while not bloodraging - and while calm, she can toggle it off to let allies' magic through. Toggling it off never works mid-rage: the blood refuses.

The sister-in-arms turns the Gray Maidens' discipline outward and fights for the shield line. Her challenge is weakened, but she carries the devotion of two orders at once, guards her wards with her own body, and cannot be turned against them. This replaces mount, cavalier's charge, mighty charge, and supreme charge.
Her challenge adds only half her cavalier level (minimum 1) to damage against the challenged foe. A sister's focus is never that narrow.

She does not choose an order - she belongs to both the order of the dragon and the order of the lion, and gains every benefit of each at the appropriate levels: the lion's regal command and the dragon's wholehearted devotion to the group. She trades her mount for this. Infantry, like the sisters she fights beside.
The sister's bloodline of loyalty: allies strike her challenge target harder, her presence shields them, and at the heights of the craft she commands the whole line at once.
Perception and Lore (Nature) become class skills. The dragon's Survival is a hunter's skill; in the Worldwound it falls to Lore (Nature).
While her challenge is active, every ally within 30 feet gains a circumstance bonus on attack rolls against her challenge target, growing with her cavalier level.
Bonus on attack rolls against the sister's challenge target.

While her challenge is active, allies within 30 feet gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and on saving throws, rising to +3 at 8th level and +4 at 14th. (Tabletop port: Wrath has no aid another action - a sister's aid is simply always there.)
Circumstance bonus to AC and saves while the sister's challenge holds.
Standard action: every ally within 30 feet (herself included) gains +2 dodge AC and +2 morale on attack rolls for 1 round. The plan is simple; the execution is everything.
+2 dodge AC and +2 morale on attack rolls.

Standard action against one enemy: every ally within 30 feet gains +2 dodge AC for 1 round, and each ally beside the mark strikes it immediately. (Tabletop port: the tabletop moves every ally; Wrath settles for the blows.)
She gains the Divine Guardian's bodyguard training: when a ward beside her is attacked, she interposes. (Wrath has no Bodyguard feat; the guardian's version stands in.)

+2 on Will saves against compulsion and mind-affecting effects that would compel her to attack or betray her allies, +1 more every 4 levels beyond 4th. They tried to make her a weapon against her sisters. They failed.
Lion's call becomes a move action, and she learns Dragon's Strategy and Act as One. She replaces mighty charge - a commander's voice carries further than one good hit.
At 20th level, lion's call becomes a swift action.
The lion's roar, delivered without breaking stride.
The lion's roar, a word in battle.

The carousel's whole style is the charge. She provokes no attacks of opportunity while charging, her mount ignores difficult terrain, her allies never block her path, and with practice one charge becomes several. This replaces banner, mighty charge, and supreme charge.
Gains Carousel Charge: a standard-action charge at double speed whose rider provokes no attacks of opportunity.
Charge the target: move at double speed and make a single charge attack. While charging she provokes no attacks of opportunity.
While charging she does not provoke attacks of opportunity. A rider at full gallop is a hard target.
After she charges this round, she may immediately charge a different enemy as a free action. Once per round. This replaces cavalier's charge - the line is upgraded, not lost.
A free-action charge against a new enemy. Requires a charge this round; once per round.
A charge this round has primed the wheel.
The wheel has already turned this round.
Her mount ignores difficult terrain - magical mud, grease and entangling ground do not slow the gallop - and gains +2 on all saving throws. Her charges ignore difficult terrain as well.
Ignores difficult terrain; +2 on all saving throws.
Allies never block her charge line - she threads the gaps in her own formation at full gallop. This replaces banner; a standard is a thing for soldiers who stand still.
The wheel no longer needs priming: once per round, any round, she may wheel. Her charges gain +2 on attack rolls. This replaces mighty charge.
+2 morale on attack rolls while charging.
The wheel knows no limit - every round is one long charge. This replaces supreme charge.

Not every priest serves at an altar. The cardinal serves at a table - councils, courts, and cloistered backrooms where the church's true business is done. She keeps her spells and her devotion, but her calling is the world: she trains as a scholar and a schemer rather than a soldier of the faith, learning 6 skill ranks per level instead of the usual 2 and counting Trickery among her class skills. The price of that education is paid in steel - she wears only light armor and never a shield, fights with a scholar's grace rather than a crusader's (her attack bonus grows as slowly as a wizard's), keeps only a single domain, and can no longer convert her prepared spells into healing or harm on the fly.

She gains 6 skill ranks per level instead of 2, and Trickery counts as a class skill. In the wider world her gift for deception and local knowledge folds into the Persuasion and Knowledge skills clerics already command. Her base attack bonus from cleric levels is that of a wizard.

The solipsist preaches a congregation of one. He cannot cast helpful spells on others or channel energy, but from 8th level every spell he casts on himself settles twice, the echo stacking with the original and with everything else. He also gains martial weapon proficiency, a bonus combat feat, and scaling bonuses to attack rolls and hit points.

Every cleric spell that could target an ally can now only target him; hostile targets are unaffected, so cure spells still burn undead. The communal versions of ally-affecting spells are denied to him altogether. In exchange he never gains channel energy. The doubling of his blessings is a separate gift and does not arrive until 8th level.

From 8th level every spell the solipsist casts on himself lays its blessings down twice. The echo is untyped, stacks with the original, and cannot be overridden by same-type effects; healing spells roll twice. Personal-range blessings echo as well, including divine power and righteous might. The echo fires only when he is both caster and target, so blessings laid on him by others are never doubled.

A congregation of one must be its own church militant. The solipsist trains with martial weapons and gains one bonus combat feat chosen from the fighter's list. What he cannot receive from others, he must be able to do himself.

Self-reliance sharpens the hand that guides it. The solipsist gains a +1 untyped bonus on his attack rolls, rising to +2 at 15th level. It stacks with everything, for it comes from no school of magic - only from never once having been able to count on anyone else.
A body that heals only itself learns to hold together. The solipsist gains +5 hit points, rising to +10 at 20th level - untyped and stackable, like everything he keeps for himself.

A shaman with this totem calls upon the proud lion, imposing and majestic, the mighty leader of deadly hunters. Her wild shape bends toward the great cats: she takes the feline form early and in its fiercest incarnation, while her other forms come more slowly than a common druid's. She can adopt an aspect of the lion while keeping her own shape, her summons fight with the pride's strength behind them, and her steady discipline earns her feats a lesser druid would never spare the time for.

She may adopt one aspect of her totem while retaining her normal form: the pride's tireless movement, its senses (scent), or its weapons (a bite attack). Only one aspect can be worn at a time, and donning one sheds the others. Each aspect grows stronger at 8th level and again at 14th. This replaces woodland stride.

The pride runs down its prey across the whole of the plain. While this aspect is worn, the lion shaman gains a +10 enhancement bonus to her movement speed and a +1 dodge bonus to AC - rising to +20 and +2 at 8th level, and +30 and +3 at 14th.

Nothing moves on the savanna without the pride knowing. While this aspect is worn, the lion shaman gains the scent ability and a +1 bonus on Will and Reflex saves - rising to +2 at 8th level and +3 at 14th.
The lion's jaws answer for her. While this aspect is worn, the lion shaman gains a bite natural attack and a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls - rising to +2 at 8th level and +3 at 14th.

She gains the smilodon as a wild shape form two levels before a common druid's shapes begin, with mightier incarnations arriving at 8th and 14th level. Her other wild shapes, animal and elemental alike, come two levels later than a common druid's.

The pride answers when she calls. The lion shaman gains Augment Summoning - every creature she summons with summon nature's ally fights with the pride's strength: +4 Strength and +4 Constitution. This replaces resist nature's lure.

The lion's patience is a discipline. At 9th level and every four levels thereafter, the lion shaman gains a bonus feat: Dodge, Iron Will, Improved Iron Will, or Skill Focus (Acrobatics). This replaces venom immunity.

The true shape druid lives in his form rather than borrowing it. His wild shape does not lapse and costs nothing to change, he casts from within it with armor and shield still on, and the beast lends its might to his magic. This replaces spellcasting above 4th level and detect magic.

While Beast Soul is active his wild shape does not lapse, and changing form costs no action. He casts druid spells while shaped, as Natural Spell, and keeps the full armor class of his worn armor and shield. His 1st-4th level spell slots increase by one at every odd level from 5th, to +8 by 19th, and while shaped his spells cast at +1 caster level per 2 druid levels - +10 at 20th level, an effective caster level of 30.
Toggle the permanence of the wild shape. While on, the druid's current form is replenished before it can expire; while off, forms lapse on their natural duration.

His wild shape is a full menagerie rather than a short list: bear and elephant to hold a line, smilodon, wolf, and wolverine to hunt, spider to bind, manticore to strike from afar, fey to weave, griffon to fly, boar and dinosaur for the uglier work. Changing form is a free action. This replaces the druid's wild shape.
The menagerie's fiercer tier unlocks: the greater incarnations of every form in his stable.
The menagerie's final tier unlocks: the mightiest incarnations of every form in his stable.

The polearm master is schooled in the ancient wisdom that enemies are best faced at the end of a long striking pole, lashing like a serpent before clumsy swords and axes can even be brought to bear. He trades the fighter's armor training and weapon versatility entirely: his craft is the spear, the glaive, the halberd - and nothing else. In exchange his polearms strike harder and truer than any other fighter's weapons, his reach becomes a wall his enemies break against, and his allies fight behind the finest hedge of steel on the battlefield.

The polearm master fights comfortably at bad distances. He gains a bonus on attack rolls with polearms against adjacent enemies: +1 at 2nd level, rising by 1 for every four levels beyond 2nd, to a maximum of +5 at 18th. This replaces bravery.

A readied polearm punishes those who close with it. The polearm master gains a bonus on attacks of opportunity he makes with a spear or polearm: +1 at 3rd level, rising by 1 for every four levels beyond 3rd, to a maximum of +5 at 19th. This replaces armor training 1 through 4.

The polearm is the only weapon the polearm master needs. He gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with spears and polearms (including glaives, bardiches, fauchards and scythes) while wielding one, increasing by 1 at 9th, 13th and 17th level. This replaces weapon training.

The polearm master chooses his angles, not his position. He gains a +2 bonus on attack rolls against any target that at least one of his allies threatens - wherever he stands relative to it, he is effectively flanking. This replaces weapon training 2.
The butt of a polearm sweeps legs and shoves chests. The polearm master gains a +2 bonus on trip and bull rush maneuvers he makes while wielding a spear or polearm. This replaces weapon training 3.

While wielding a polearm he gains a +2 dodge bonus to his armor class. In turn-based combat only, when an adjacent enemy's melee attack against him resolves, he takes a 5-foot step away once per round. (Five-foot steps do not exist in real-time-with-pause mode; there the constant footwork alone stands.) This replaces weapon training 4.

As a swift action he braces his weapon for 1 round. While braced, allies within 10 feet of him gain a +2 shield bonus to AC against attacks from enemies within his reach, and damage dealt to them by such enemies is reduced by 5. This replaces armor mastery.

A strategic soldier is a master of positioning and teamwork in combat. Where other fighters polish their own steel, the strategic soldier polishes the battle itself: he stands where his presence doubles his allies, steps out of every blow's path, and answers every wound dealt to his friends with steel of his own. The price is the fighter's own resilience - no bravery, no armor training, no armor mastery - for he has made himself the keystone of the line rather than its wall.

The strategic soldier fights from whichever square the fight needs him in. He gains a +2 bonus on attack rolls against any target that at least one of his allies threatens - wherever he stands relative to it, he is effectively flanking. This replaces the bonus combat feat gained at 1st level.
The strategic soldier is already elsewhere by the time the blow lands. He gains the Mobility feat, adding his footwork to his defense when he moves through his enemies' reach. This replaces bravery.

The strategic soldier can take the damage dealt by an attack aimed at an ally. He gains the Bodyguard and In Harm's Way abilities: when an adjacent ally is attacked, he may use his reaction to aid its defense and take the blow in its place. This replaces armor training 1.
Standing beside the strategic soldier is standing behind a shield. Allies within 5 feet of him gain a +2 dodge bonus to their armor class. This replaces armor training 2.

Once per round, the strategic soldier can eschew defense for one round of dangerous strikes: as a swift action he gains +5 on attack and damage rolls for 1 round - and a -5 penalty to his own armor class, for every blade that finds him in that round finds flesh. This replaces armor training 3.

As a standard action, the strategic soldier makes a single attack that leaves its target reeling: he strikes, and every ally threatening the target attacks it in the same breath. The target must be no more than one size category larger than the soldier. This replaces armor training 4.

Wounding the strategic soldier's allies is a mistake he answers personally: when an enemy damages an ally, he may make an attack of opportunity against that enemy - once per round, requiring him to threaten it and to have an attack of opportunity remaining, which the strike consumes. This replaces armor mastery.

The exoticist trains only in exotic weapons - bastard swords, estocs, urgroshes, fauchards, and their like - but within that narrow field he is without equal. His weapon training applies to exotic weapons alone.

The exoticist is proficient with every exotic weapon in the game: bastard swords, dueling swords, dwarven waraxes, elven curved blades, estocs, falcata, fauchards, sawtooth sabres, two-bladed swords, double axes, dwarven urgroshes, gnome hooked hammers, repeating crossbows, shuriken, sling staffs, and the monk's exotic arsenal of sai, kama, tongi, siangham and nunchaku.

The exoticist's craft admits only the strange. He gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with exotic weapons while wielding one, increasing by 1 at 9th, 13th and 17th level. This replaces weapon training.

The qinggong monk trades every fixed gift of her order for choice. Where other monks receive still mind, fast movement, and purity of body as their masters decreed, she channels that training into her ki instead - three extra ki powers of her choosing by 5th level, drawn from the full library: true strikes and restorations, barkskin and abundant steps, invisibility and dragon's breath, true sight, even holy aura. Her order calls it undisciplined. She calls it knowing exactly what she needs and when.
By sheer discipline the monk bends light around herself, as the invisibility spell. Cost: 2 ki. Requires monk level 8.
The monk's ki burns poison from a creature's body, as the neutralize poison spell. Cost: 2 ki. Requires monk level 8.
The monk's ki frees a creature from all restraints, as the freedom of movement spell. Cost: 2 ki. Requires monk level 10.
The monk's perfected ki pours out as a mantle of sacred light, as the holy aura spell. Cost: 4 ki. Requires monk level 16.
The monk draws a deep breath from the well of her ki and exhales a roaring torrent of dragonfire, as the dragon's breath spell. Cost: 2 ki. Requires monk level 8.
The monk's ki stills her mind until her eyes cut through every veil - illusions, disguises, concealment - as the true seeing spell. Cost: 2 ki. Requires monk level 10.
The monk's ki swells until she towers over the battlefield, a presence out of nightmare that turns her enemies' courage to water, as the frightful aspect spell. Cost: 3 ki. Requires monk level 16.
The hammerfist gives up nearly everything her order holds sacred to perfect one devastating strike. This replaces flurry of blows, stunning fist, and evasion.

The hammerfist monk gives up the flurry for one perfect blow. Once per round, her first unarmed strike to connect carries the full weight of her training, dealing 2 extra damage plus 1 1/2 times her monk level. This replaces flurry of blows and stunning fist.

From 9th level, the hammerfist's first unarmed strike to connect in each attack sequence rolls through the target like thunder after lightning: it slams them with a free trip attempt that costs no action and provokes no attack of opportunity. This replaces improved evasion.

The venomblood wins by attrition rather than coordination. Every bite of her blade leaves poison behind, and the dose deepens at 12th and 16th level. This replaces hunter tactics, teamwork feats, woodland stride, and one with the wild.

Once per round her first weapon attack that hits injects venom: the target must pass a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half hunter level + Wisdom) or take 1d2 Constitution damage, rising to 1d4 from 12th level and 1d6 from 16th. The strain burns out after a round, so each round's first hit brings a fresh dose and a fresh save. The venom is supernatural and works on creatures immune to poison, though they gain +4 on the save. This replaces hunter tactics and the teamwork-feat progression.
At 6th level, the venomblood's blood runs so thick with venom that she is simply immune to poison. This replaces woodland stride.
At 9th level, the venomblood's venom reaches the nerves: a target that fails its save against Serpent's Gift is also sickened for 1 round. This replaces one with the wild.
Serpent venom burning through the veins: 1d2 Constitution damage as it enters the blood - rising to 1d4 at 12th level and 1d6 at 16th. The strain burns out after a round.
The venom has found the muscles: 1d2 Dexterity damage as it enters the blood. The strain burns out after a round.

At 12th level the venom in the venomblood's blood has had twelve years to concentrate. Serpent's Gift now deals 1d4 Constitution damage instead of 1d2, and a target that fails its save also takes 1d2 Dexterity damage as the toxin reaches the muscles.

At 16th level the venom stops being a nuisance and starts being a sentence. Serpent's Gift now deals 1d6 Constitution damage, and the sickening that Neurotoxin inflicts on a failed save becomes nausea instead - a target that fails cannot act at all for a round.

The riftstalker's companion never came back through the rift with her; it waits unseen between worlds. Her first blow marks the prey, and each round she may give the beast one directive. This replaces her animal companion, raise companion, hunter tactics, teamwork feats, and one with the wild.

Once per round her first attack that hits brands the target with a rift mark for 1 minute. Only one creature can bear the mark at a time; marking new prey strips it from the old. The mark grants nothing by itself - it is the tether through which the beast in the rift can reach. This replaces the animal companion.
At 2nd level, the riftstalker has nothing to wait for and no one to slow her down: her land speed increases by 10 feet. This replaces the teamwork-feat progression.
Branded by the riftstalker's mark: the beast in the rift can be guided to strike the branded creature.

Opens the command menu; only directives the beast has learned can be given. As a swift action she directs the beast to strike a creature bearing her rift mark: an attack roll of d20 + hunter level + Wisdom modifier against the target's AC. On a hit it deals 1d4 + half her hunter level in damage that ignores damage reduction (1d5 at 3rd level, 1d6 at 4th) and shakes the target for 1 round. The beast takes one directive per round. This replaces hunter tactics.
At 5th level, the beast circles her through the rift: the riftstalker gains a +2 dodge bonus to AC against attacks made by the creature bearing her rift mark. This replaces one with the wild.

At 4th level and every four levels thereafter (8th, 12th, 16th, and 20th) she teaches the beast a new directive of her choice from the list below. Learned commands are given through the Guided Command menu; unlearned entries are listed but do nothing. Each is a swift action aimed at a creature bearing her rift mark, resolved with the beast's attack roll (d20 + hunter level + Wisdom) against the target's AC unless noted. The beast takes one directive per round. This replaces raise companion and one with the wild.

The beast tears in with its full weight: on a hit, the mauling deals 2d6 plus half the riftstalker's hunter level in raw damage that no damage reduction blunts. The beast only grows strong enough for this at 12th level.
The beast's claws catch and hold: on a hit, the target is entangled for one round.
The beast shows itself for a single heartbeat: on a hit, the target must pass a Will save or be frightened for one round.
No strike - the beast interposes itself between the riftstalker and the marked creature: until the start of her next turn she gains a +4 dodge bonus to AC against the marked creature's attacks.
Claws across the eyes that are not there: on a hit, the target must pass a Fortitude save or be blinded for one round.
The unseen mauling drains more than blood: on a hit, the target must pass a Fortitude save or be fatigued for one minute.
The beast strikes the legs out from under the target's rhythm: on a hit, the target must pass a Fortitude save or be staggered for one round.
The beast's claws leave the target's movements ragged: on a hit, the target takes a -2 penalty on its attack rolls for one minute.
The beast in the rift has already been given its directive this round.
The unseen beast interposes itself: +4 dodge AC against the marked creature's attacks, until the start of her next turn.
Claws out of nowhere have left the target's movements ragged: -2 on attack rolls for one minute.
The beast seizes the target bodily through the rift: on a hit, the target must pass a Will save or be paralyzed for one round.

The beast erupts through the rift at the marked prey in a spray of nothing and teeth: on a hit, the marked target must pass a Will save or be frightened for one round, and every other enemy within 10 feet of it must pass a Will save or be shaken for one round.

A verminous hunter calls on the ceaseless, single-minded dedication of vermin to hunt and overwhelm her prey. Where other hunters invoke the cunning of alpha predators, she reaches out to the spider instead of the monkey, the mantis instead of the snake, the moth instead of the owl. She takes a vermin companion, takes on vermin aspects in place of animal focus, and walks through the swarm untouched. Perfect for those who have become something less - and something more - than human.

At 1st level, a verminous hunter must choose a vermin companion. In these lands, that means the giant centipede - the only creeping thing the wild offers to walk beside her. This alters the animal companion.

The verminous hunter takes on the aspect of a vermin - a permanent gift of the hive, chosen at 1st level, with a second aspect at 8th and a third at 15th. Each aspect's bonus improves at 8th and again at 15th level. This replaces animal focus.
The worker's ceaseless strength: +1 on attack and damage rolls, improving to +2 at 8th level and +3 at 15th.
The carapace: +2 natural armor, improving to +4 at 8th level and +6 at 15th.
The striking forelimbs: +2 on attacks of opportunity, improving to +4 at 8th level and +6 at 15th.
The seizing claws: +2 on combat maneuver rolls, improving to +4 at 8th level and +6 at 15th.

The flesh that waits: 50% chance to treat any critical hit or sneak attack as a normal hit, as the fortification armor special ability. (The tabletop's 25/50/75 scaling is flattened - the engine's fortification takes a single fixed value.)

At 5th level, the verminous hunter has walked with the swarm so long that their weapons no longer touch her: she is immune to poison and disease, the swarm's venom and filth. This replaces woodland stride.

Opens the construct's core command menu. Each core the crafter has learned can be armed from here; arming one clears the others, and casting this directly returns the construct to the Basic core. A core listed in the menu but not yet learned does nothing. Cores are armed before deployment.

Opens the construct's program command menu. Each program the crafter has learned can be set from here - setting one clears the others; casting this directly returns to the Basic program. A program listed in the menu but not yet learned is an empty entry and does nothing. The program governs how the deployed construct behaves.

There is a sect of inquisitors who believe it is not enough to hunt the enemies of the church - one must also devour those enemies' sins. More benign versions believe sin is taken out of the world when it is devoured, denying the enemy's soul to its god. Consuming sins empowers the sin eater, at least for a time. In the Worldwound, that is not theology - that is lunch. She trades her domain for the feast.

When her own attack kills an enemy she devours its sins and heals 1d8 + her inquisitor level, the bonus capped at +5. The healing improves to 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 9th, and 4d8 at 13th, with caps of +10, +15, and +20. She can eat the sins of a given enemy only once, and only creatures of Intelligence 3 or greater have sins worth eating. This replaces domain.

At 6th level each sin she eats also empowers her for 1 minute, granting a +1 circumstance bonus on attack rolls and saving throws. (The tabletop's speak-with-dead clause has no counterpart here; adapted from the archetype's own creed that consuming sins empowers the sin eater for a time.) This replaces the 6th-level bonus teamwork feat.
The devoured sins burn briefly in her veins: +1 circumstance bonus on attack rolls and saving throws for one minute.

The doomsayer perfects a single discipline: the pronouncement of doom. Her condemnations linger on the condemned and weigh on everyone nearby. This replaces judgments, solo tactics, teamwork feats, stalwart, exploit weakness, and true judgment.

As a swift action she pronounces doom on a creature: a Persuasion check against 10 + the target's level + its Wisdom modifier. On a success the target is shaken for 1 minute and becomes her condemned, granting her +1 on attack rolls against it (+2 at 9th level, +3 at 17th); only one creature can be condemned at a time. At 5th level, pronouncing doom on a shaken target frightens it for 3 rounds instead. At 12th, a frightened target is also staggered for 1 round. At 17th no check is required. This replaces judgments, including second judgment, third judgment, and true judgment.

Every blow lands like a gavel. When her weapon attack hits, the victim must weather a free Persuasion check made to intimidate against 10 + its level + its Wisdom modifier; on a success it is shaken for 1 round (2 rounds from 10th level). This replaces solo tactics and all bonus teamwork feats.

Enemies within 15 feet take a -2 penalty on attack rolls and saving throws made against her, deepening to -3 at 12th level and -4 at 16th. This is the weight of doom, not fear: no save is allowed, and creatures immune to fear still feel it. This replaces second judgment.

When her condemned dies, every enemy within 30 feet hears the sentence close: each must succeed at a Will save (10 + half her inquisitor level + her Wisdom modifier) or be shaken for 1 minute. With the Final Verdict (17th level), the echo carries 50 feet. This replaces stalwart.

At 14th level, the condemned wears the sentence where all can see it: while marked, the creature takes a -2 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws and Armor Class - against her and against everyone else, deepening to -3 from 17th level. This replaces exploit weakness.
At 16th level, her presence deepens: the reach of Dread Mien extends to 30 feet. This replaces third judgment.

At 17th level, her pronouncements no longer require a check - when she reads a creature its sentence, the sentence is simply read, and only the fear that follows can be resisted. Her Death's Echo also carries further, reaching 50 feet. This replaces true judgment.
The doomsayer has read this creature its sentence. It stands condemned.
The doomsayer has read this creature its sentence, and the sentence is ruin: -2 on attack rolls, saving throws and Armor Class until the sentence is executed or she condemns another.

The doomsayer has read this creature its sentence, and the sentence is ruin: -3 on attack rolls, saving throws and Armor Class until the sentence is executed or she condemns another. She has been reading sentences a long time, and this one is heavier than the ones she used to write.
Verdicts unspoken hang about the doomsayer; within her mien, enemies take a penalty on attack rolls and saving throws made against her: -2, or -3 from her 12th level and -4 from her 16th.

The kinetic blast detonates violently in a 20-foot radius, hitting every enemy in the area. The explosion accepts 3 points of burn. This is a form infusion usable with every kinetic blast possessed; it is learned through the infusion selection at 9th level or above. (Tabletop port: the 5th-level form infusion, previously missing from the game.)
The unstable kineticist's gate never settled. Every blast she throws risks a wild surge, and no one chooses what it does. This replaces gather power and elemental overflow.

Every kinetic blast she throws has a 25% chance of a surge. Roll d6: 1 Eruption - the target takes an extra 1d6 per 3 kineticist levels; 2 Chain Arc - enemies within 10 feet take 1d6 per 4 levels; 3 Violent Discharge - the target is shaken for 1 round; 4 Rebound - she takes 1d6 per 4 levels; 5 Overcharge - Eruption and the discharge both; 6 Null Surge - nothing happens. This replaces gather power.
At 8th level she has learned to shrug off the bite: Rebound results on her surge table become Null Surges instead.
At 16th level the gate's instability peaks: the chance of a surge on each of her kinetic blasts rises to 50%.

While any kineticist can learn the rudiments of healing, some are virtuosos of the curative arts. The kinetic chirurgeon trades her entire shaping discipline - infusions, metakinesis, infusion specialization - for the healer's craft: her touch knits flesh with raw elemental force, and as she grows, her healing learns to mend what flesh alone cannot.

A touch heals a willing creature for 1d6 + Constitution modifier per 2 kineticist levels, and costs 1 burn; if she cannot accept the burn, the healing does not occur. Each use also cures one condition, from fatigued and shaken at 3rd level up to stunned at 9th. Metahealer adds one extra die at 5th level, two at 11th, three at 17th, and at 17th the use heals her as well. This replaces infusions and infusion specialization.

At 13th level she learns to mend herself in an instant: as a swift action, she may use kinetic healer on herself, at the normal cost of 1 point of burn. This replaces metakinesis (empower, maximize and quicken).
At 5th level, her healing deepens: kinetic healer rolls one additional healing die. This becomes two additional dice at 11th level and three at 17th.
At 17th level, the same use of kinetic healer mends both her target and herself.

The stormcaller is the wind given a rider: faster than any other kineticist and throwing more bolts, each carrying less of the storm. Her lightning is true lightning. This replaces elemental defense and any second element.

Her land speed increases by 10 feet. She also gains a swift version of every air-family kinetic blast she possesses - a free action usable once per round with the damage dice halved. Her electricity is the storm's own and ignores electricity immunity and resistance. This replaces enveloping winds and the expanded element line.
At 5th level, the wind pushes harder: her land speed increases by another 10 feet (20 feet total).

At 8th level, as a swift action she may blink to the side of any creature within close range - friend or foe - riding the current between one heartbeat and the next. The step carries no attack; it is pure motion.
At 12th level, she slips between the wind's moments: she may use her swift blasts twice per round.
At 16th level, the storm accepts her completely. Her swift blasts no longer halve their damage dice, and she becomes immune to electricity - the storm does not strike its own.

A free action that keeps the blast's full attack roll and typing with every damage entry's dice halved. Usable once per round, twice with Riding the Current. The round's charge is spent when the bolt is loosed; it lands or breaks on the wind, and the storm does not refund it.

As a swift action she may speak her vow over a companion (Intercession). While marked, half the damage that companion takes is transferred to her, beyond armor and beyond resistance. At mythic rank 4 the vow widens to two companions at once. A fallen vow-carrier carries nothing. Only oracles can take this mythic ability.
Speak the vow over one ally within close range (never herself): the ally gains the Mark of the Vow. A swift action, usable at will. When the vow is spoken at its capacity, the oldest mark passes on.
Her body answers for yours: half of the damage you take is transferred to her, beyond armor and beyond resistance. If she falls, the vow carries nothing.

A planar oracle has an affinity with one of the Outer Planes. She is at home on the multiple planes of the Great Beyond, and can eventually become an outsider herself. At 1st level she chooses a plane (Heaven, Hell, the Abyss, or the Maelstrom), each bound to one energy: at 3rd level she gains resistance 10 to that energy (20 at 11th), and at 20th she becomes an extraplanar creature - immune to her plane's energy, with damage reduction 10/magic. Her pilgrim's road is written in bonus spells (protection from evil, see invisibility, protection from energy, freedom of movement, dismissal, chain lightning, banishment, mind blank, elemental swarm), gained at the planar slots. This replaces her 3rd- and 7th-level revelations and her final revelation.
Choose the Outer Plane she is attuned to. This choice cannot be changed.
The archons' plane of law and good. Her attuned energy is electricity, the light of the Silver City.
The devils' plane of law and evil. Her attuned energy is fire, the endless pits of Asmodeus.
The demons' plane of chaos and evil. Her attuned energy is cold, the lightless depths of the Worldwound's masters.
The proteans' plane of pure chaos. Her attuned energy is acid, the dissolving storm at the center of the Great Beyond.
At 3rd level she gains energy resistance 10 against her chosen plane's associated energy type. This replaces the 3rd-level revelation.
At 11th level her energy resistance against her chosen plane's energy type increases to 20.

At 20th level she becomes an extraplanar creature, gaining superficial physical characteristics appropriate to natives of her chosen plane, immunity to her associated energy type, and damage reduction 10/magic. Unlike other outsiders she can still be brought back from the dead. This replaces her final revelation.

The apocryphal oracle copies wizard spells into her spells known and casts them as oracle spells. Each stolen spell permanently costs 2 maximum hit points, and the cost cannot be healed. This replaces all revelations of her mystery.
Copy one wizard spell of a level she can cast into her oracle spells known. The theft is paid for in years of her own life: each stolen spell permanently reduces her maximum hit points by 2.
A pilgrim's spell of the planes beyond, gained through the planar oracle's attunement.
A spell copied from the wizard's book into her own - a page of apocrypha. The theft permanently costs 2 maximum hit points; the price is never refunded.

The shining knight is never far from her steed. At 3rd level her mount shares her divine grace, at 5th her divine bond must be the steed, and at 11th a mounted charge against her smitten quarry forces a Will save or panics it. This replaces divine health, the weapon option of divine bond, and aura of justice.

Any mount she rides shares her conviction: the mount gains the benefit of her divine grace, adding her Charisma bonus (if any) to its saving throws. (The tabletop's Ride-skill clause has no meaning in this world - there are no Ride checks - and is cut.) This replaces divine health.

Whenever her mounted charge hits the target of her smite evil, that target must make a Will save (DC 10 + half her paladin level + Charisma modifier) or be panicked for a number of rounds equal to half her paladin level. (The tabletop's no-provoke clause has no engine here and is cut; the charge still draws attacks of opportunity.) This replaces aura of justice.

The fortunes fool swears her oath to chance rather than to order, and only the chaotic may walk her road. Every attack is a wager: a natural 1-4 misses outright, while a natural 17 or higher deals extra damage. Her damage counts as chaotic and she gains a luck bonus on saves against fear. This replaces lay on hands, mercies, smite evil, channel positive energy, and all auras.

Every weapon attack she makes rides the die. On a natural 1-4 the blow misses even if her modifiers would hit; on a natural 17 or higher it deals an extra 1d6 per two paladin levels, stacking with critical hits.
