She gains a luck bonus on saves against fear equal to her Charisma modifier, minimum +2, rather than immunity, and her physical damage counts as chaotic.
Allies within 10 feet (herself included) gain a +1 luck bonus on attack rolls. This replaces aura of courage.
+1 luck bonus on attack rolls, carried on the fool's road.

Allies within 10 feet (herself included) gain damage reduction that grows with her: 2 at 8th level, 3 at 11th, 4 at 14th, and 5 at 17th, where it stops. No weapon, no magic, no material pierces it; only damage in excess of it. This replaces aura of resolve.
Damage reduction that grows with the Fool herself - no weapon pierces it, only damage in excess of it.

Allies within 10 feet (herself included) carry her lesser blessing: their weapon hits on a natural d20 roll of 17+ deal an extra 2d6 damage - but the star spends itself when it fires, and returns only with her next turn. This replaces aura of justice.
Her weapon hits on a natural d20 roll of 17 or higher deal an extra 2d6 damage. Once it fires, the star leaves her until her next turn.
Allies within 10 feet (herself included) gain a +2 luck bonus on all saving throws. This replaces aura of faith.
+2 luck bonus on all saving throws.

Her companions within 10 feet carry Fate's Wager itself: their weapon attacks scatter on a natural 1-4 and surge on a natural 17+ with an extra 1d6 per two of her paladin levels. She already carries the wager - it does not stack with itself. This replaces aura of righteousness.
Fate's Wager rides her blows: on a natural 1-4 the attack scatters and misses; on a natural 17 or higher it deals an extra 1d6 per two paladin levels.

Many rangers are loners, but the guide walks with others - and brings them home. He forgoes the favored enemy of his peers to focus on the task at hand: a swift mark upon one foe, luck spent on a single die, a moment of perfect clarity when it matters most. His camp is a moving school of woodcraft - quick to act, sharp of eye, soft of foot - and he gives it all away. This replaces favored enemy (all ranks), hunter's bond, evasion, improved evasion, quarry, and improved quarry; master hunter remains.

Once per day, plus one additional use per three levels after 1st, he can focus on a single enemy within line of sight as a swift action. The mark holds until the target dies or he names a new focus. He gains +2 on attack and damage rolls against his focus, increasing by +2 at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (+2, +4, +6, +8, +10). This replaces favored enemy.

Swift action: mark one enemy within line of sight as his focus. The mark holds until the target dies or he names a new focus. He gains a bonus on attack and damage rolls against his focus: +2, increasing by +2 at 5th level and every five levels thereafter.
The guide has named this creature his focus. He gains a bonus on attack and damage rolls against it - and he does not miss twice.

At 4th level, the guide forms a bond with the land itself and directs others through it: he and all allies within 30 feet gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks and on Perception, Stealth, and Lore (Nature) checks - Survival in the tabletop, the wilderness skill here. This replaces hunter's bond.
+2 on initiative, Perception, Stealth, and Lore (Nature). The guide's camp is a moving school of woodcraft.

At 9th level, once per day, as a swift action, the guide wraps his next attack of the round in luck: if that attack misses, the die rolls again. The second result stands. One additional use per day at 14th and 19th level. This replaces evasion.
Swift action: his next attack this round, if it misses, is rerolled. The second result stands - even if it is worse, though only a miss can summon the luck.
His next attack roll this round that misses is rerolled. The luck spends itself when it fires.

At 11th level, once per day as a free action, the guide can have an inspired moment: until the end of his next turn his speed increases by 10 feet, he gains +4 to AC and on attack rolls, and every critical threat he scores is automatically confirmed. Twice per day at 19th level. This replaces quarry and improved quarry.
Free action: for 1 round, +10 foot speed, +4 AC, +4 on attack rolls, and every critical threat is automatically confirmed.
+10 foot speed, +4 AC, +4 on attack rolls, and every critical threat is automatically confirmed. One clear moment, spent well.
At 16th level, his luck hardens: every reroll made with ranger's luck carries a +4 luck bonus on the attack roll. This replaces improved evasion.

The wildbonded ranger has a partner instead of a favored enemy. Her companion answers from 1st level, and the bond shapes the beast itself - each species bringing its own way of fighting. This replaces favored enemy, favored terrain, evasion, and all spellcasting before 12th level.

Her animal companion carries a species bond that grows with her, improving at 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 20th level. See the bond of her chosen beast. This replaces hunter's bond; the companion itself arrives at 1st level.

The bond deepens to its second tier: the bear's ward hardens, the boar's fury doubles, the dog runs farther, the phantom elk closes the gap, the leopard's precision grows, the mastodon needs less momentum, the smilodon's stacks climb higher, the raptor's rend deepens, the pack howls wider - and the pack gains attack speed.

The bond deepens again, to its third tier - and her spells return, eight levels late. The bear wards harder, the boar heals more, the leopard strikes past concealment's edge (+2), the mastodon's impact widens, the smilodon earns an extra attack at six stacks, the raptor's rend bites 1d6, and the pack reaches 30 feet at +2/-2.

The bond deepens (fourth tier): the boar frenzies at three quarters health, the phantom elk nearly matches the real one, the mastodon needs but two rounds of momentum, the pack howls every other round - and answers a wounded ally on its own.

The bond completes (fifth tier): the bear's ward is iron, the boar's frenzy is a storm, the phantom elk is the elk, the leopard's precision is 5d6, the smilodon hunts with twelve stacks of bloodshed, the raptor's rend is 1d8, the wolf answers any enemy that fights beside it - and the triceratops's second charge hits like the first.
The bond rides the beast: it grows with the ranger's level.
Mauled by the bear: -10 speed, and its blows against the bear's master land softer.
The bear is ready to answer its master's strike against a mauled enemy - once per round.
The boar's fury, boiled over: bonus damage on every strike, a second wind already spent, and fear forgotten.
The dog has marked this creature as its prey. When its master strikes the prey, the dog runs; when the dog has it down, the master strikes true.
Prone beneath the hound: the ranger gains a bonus on attack and damage rolls against this creature.
The master struck the prey - the dog gains +15 speed for a round.
Marked by the leopard. The ranger's attacks against this creature deal bonus precision damage.
The leopard watches for a vulnerable moment - once per round it can mark.
The mastodon is moving, and something is about to break.
Caught in the mastodon's impact: -10 speed.
The smilodon's consecutive strikes build: +1 damage per two stacks. Switch targets and it is lost.
Six stacks of bloodshed: the smilodon strikes with an extra attack each round while the streak holds.
The raptor's talons have done their work. The ranger's next attack consumes every stack.
The rending relay pays off: -2 AC for a round.
The wolf's howl rides her: bonuses against enemies adjacent to the wolf, and from the second tier, attack speed. Enemies beset by two of the pack suffer.
After its charge, the triceratops plants itself: bonus AC, unable to be tripped, and allies nearby gain +2 AC.
The bulwark is broken into momentum: +10 speed, and its next hit deals +2d6.
Riding the bond: +10 speed, and mounted charges hit harder as they grow together.
The centipede's venom, deepened by every strike of its master: -1 to all saves per rank.
The monitor's bite lingers - and the beast drinks the strength of it.
The wolf watches - once per round, an enemy that fights beside it answers to fang and master alike.
Swift action: command the triceratops to end its bulwark and ready a second charge (+10 speed; its next hit deals +2d6).

Swift action, the hound's: command the dog to designate one enemy as its Prey. When she strikes the prey the hound gains +15 speed for a round, and while the prey is prone she gains a bonus on attack and damage rolls against it. The hound keeps its prey until she commands a new one.

Not all rogues live in the city. Scouts roam the wilderness - bandits, trailblazers, companions to rangers and barbarians - and they kill on the move. Her charge lands like an ambush, and a scout who has covered ground strikes as if from hiding. This replaces uncanny dodge and improved uncanny dodge; everything else about the rogue is untouched.

At 4th level, whenever the scout makes a charge, her attack treats the target as flat-footed - sneak attack damage lands, and the target's Dexterity bonus to AC is denied. Foes with uncanny dodge are immune to this ability. This replaces uncanny dodge.

At 8th level, whenever the scout moves more than 10 feet in a round and makes an attack, the attack treats the target as flat-footed - but only the first attack she makes that round. Foes with uncanny dodge are immune to this ability. This replaces improved uncanny dodge.
The steel rain rogue throws instead of knifing. Javelins, axes, and darts fly from thirty feet away, with quick hands and a cruel ricochet. This replaces trapfinding and danger sense.
At 1st level, she gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls with thrown weapons. The bonus increases to +2 at 8th level and +3 at 16th. This replaces trapfinding.
At 6th level, she adds her Dexterity modifier to damage rolls with thrown weapons, on top of the Strength the throw already carries. Her arm was always the point.

At 12th level, once per round, when she kills a creature with a thrown weapon, the blade comes back clean and goes out again: an immediate free attack at the nearest living enemy within 30 feet. On a hit, the returning throw deals 1d6 + her Dexterity modifier.
Her hands only know the throw. She takes a -2 penalty on attack rolls with any weapon that is not a thrown weapon - blades and bows alike. The price of the Steel Rain.

The anatomist studies her enemies instead of simply fighting them. Near misses reveal a foe's weaknesses, which she never forgets, and she can trade her own defense for a better opening. This replaces trapfinding and danger sense.

Whenever she misses with an attack that needed a high natural roll to hit, she finds a seam: a permanent, stacking +1 bonus on attack rolls against that enemy. The qualifying roll is 16 at 1st level, dropping by 1 every three levels to 10 at 18th. This replaces trapfinding.
The anatomist has found the seams in this creature's armor: a stacking +1 bonus on her attack rolls against it. She does not forget.

At 8th level, her study turns to how enemies defend themselves. Whenever she attacks a spellcaster, she gains spell resistance (4 + her rogue level) for 1 round. Whenever she damages an enemy that has damage reduction, she deals +1 additional damage per five rogue levels - the same reading, not stackable.
Her study of the caster's craft guards her: spell resistance 4 + her rogue level, for as long as she keeps attacking spellcasters.
At 16th level, once per round, when she hits an enemy carrying five or more of her seams, the strike is an automatic critical. She has known where the knife goes for a while now.

Swift action: she drops her guard (-6 AC for 1 round) to find an opening - her next attack this round applies a seam to its target whether it hits or misses. No roll needed; the opening is taken, not given. If she does not attack, the guard was simply spent.
Her guard is spent: -6 AC, and her next attack this round will find a seam whether it lands or not.

At 12th level, against enemies carrying her seams, she reads the telegraphs before they move: a +2 dodge bonus to AC against every one of them. The longer she has studied a thing, the less it can surprise her.

The chimera witch keeps a beast instead of a familiar. Whenever her companion kills a creature type it has not yet eaten, it gains a permanent trait from that flesh - twelve types in all. This replaces her familiar, eight of her ten hex levels, and one spell slot per spell level from 6th level onward. (Prestige classes that advance the witch spellbook do not advance this thinned spellbook.)
Choose the beast the witch bonds with. It grows with her full class level and carries the chimera's diet: whatever it kills, it takes a piece of.

The witch's bond is not a familiar's whisper but a beast's hunger. When her companion kills a creature of a type it has not yet eaten, it takes a piece of the kill and grows a permanent trait from that flesh. Humanoids leave no piece worth taking, and the witch's own kills are hers, not the beast's.
Strange meat reshapes strange minds. The beast gains a +2 insight bonus on Will saves.
The beast has eaten aberration flesh and grown alien minds.
Kinship, devoured. The beast's speed increases by 10 feet.
The beast has eaten animal flesh and found it familiar.
Gears and plating settle in the gut. The beast gains damage reduction 2/adamantine.
The beast has eaten construct parts and digested stone.
Something old and precise wakes behind its eyes. The beast gains a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls.
The beast has eaten dragon flesh and dreams of hoards.
Caprice, swallowed whole. The beast gains a +2 insight bonus on Reflex saves.
The beast has eaten fey flesh and learned to laugh at danger.
The moon's mark, eaten. The beast gains damage reduction 2/silver.
The beast has eaten lycanthrope flesh and carries the moon's mark.
It eats another monster and wears it. The beast gains a +2 natural armor bonus to AC.
The beast has eaten magical beast flesh and wears the monster now.
Predator eats predator. The beast gains a +2 competence bonus on initiative checks.
The beast has eaten monstrous humanoid flesh and hunts first.
The blood of another world burns hot. The beast gains fire resistance 10.
The beast has eaten outsider flesh and its blood burns.
Green stubbornness, chewed and kept. The beast gains a +2 insight bonus on Fortitude saves.
The beast has eaten plant matter and grown patient roots.
Death itself, tasted. The beast gains a +1 insight bonus on all saving throws.
The beast has eaten undead flesh and been greeted by the grave.
A thousand small lessons in escape. The beast becomes immune to the entangled condition.
The beast has eaten vermin and knows how small things slip free.

Among witches, there are those who devote themselves to the care of others and restrict their practices to the healing arts. They often take the place of clerics in rural communities, wandering the countryside and tending to the sick.
The hedge witch trades the hexes she would learn at 4th and 8th level for the healer's true arts: her prepared spells can be channeled into healing, and she can draw poison and disease out of the afflicted - taking their pain into herself.

She can lose any prepared spell that is not a cantrip to cast any cure spell of the same level or lower - from cure light wounds to mass heal - even if she does not know that cure spell. (Regenerate is not in the game; 7th-level slots convert to heal instead, which the same-or-lower rule allows.)

As a standard action she touches a diseased or poisoned creature and removes all poisons and diseases from it. She suffers the remembered pain, taking 2d6 damage immediately. (Tabletop port: the original redirects the victim's next failed save to the witch; Wrath does not expose affliction internals, so the port cures outright and charges a fixed pain instead.)
The hedge witch has drawn an affliction out of someone else; its last echo hurts her still.

Considered bringers of fortune and prosperity, a jiuweihu is a kitsune shaman who has been blessed with multiple tails by the spirits of unseen kami. In rare cases, evil jiuweihu who are instead championed by wicked oni are created.
The jiuweihu trades her spirit animal for a star jewel - the spirit rests in a grape-sized gem that cannot be slain - and grows a new magical tail at 1st level and every two levels thereafter, each granting a spell-like ability. Only kitsune may take this archetype.
(Tabletop port: the game embeds shaman spirit magic inside each spirit, so the tabletop's spirit-magic trade could not be excised - the jiuweihu keeps her spirit magic, and the port is up one trade as a result.)

The jiuweihu's spirit rests in a star-cut jewel the size of a grape. It cannot be slain, charmed, or frightened, and needs no feeding. She gains a +1 luck bonus on all saving throws. (Tabletop port: the original jewel-bound lets the familiar transform into an item, orbit like an ioun stone, and gain hardness. The game has no item-form familiars, so the spirit stays in the jewel and grants its fortune.)

The ninth tail is the one the myths agree on: it belongs to the spirit, not the fox. She chooses one of her Magical Tail spell-like abilities and can use it one additional time per day. She cannot choose the same tail twice.

The spirit-ridden lost the argument with the spirits, and they moved in. She gives up her spells, her hexes, her spirit animal, and her spirit. In exchange she can let one of them take the reins as a swift action, fighting as another class and manifesting its arms and armor while she wears nothing of her own.

Choose a spirit of a dead hero to inhabit the shaman's body. Each spirit can be channeled at will as a swift action: while channeled she fights as that spirit's class at her shaman level minus two, with no reduction for the first two levels, and if her body is bare the spirit's equipment manifests on her. Only one spirit can hold the reins at a time. The Weapon Saint and the Red Warlord answer a first call; the Barefoot Master and the Cutthroat come at 6th level, the Grey Hunter at 12th, the First Knight at 18th.

A swordsman who died mid-perfect-cut and never accepted it. While the Saint holds the reins she fights as a FIGHTER: all armor and shield proficiencies, a fighter's full attack progression, and a growing edge on attack and damage rolls (+1 per four effective levels).

A warlord whose last battle never ended. While the Warlord holds the reins she fights as a barbarian: martial weapons, a barbarian's full attack progression, and Strength and Constitution surging by +2, rising to +4 and +6 as she grows, with +2 on Will saves and a cost of 2 points of armor class.

An ascetic who forgot to stop walking. While the Master holds the reins she fights as a MONK: the monk's weapon arts, a slowly climbing dodge bonus to armor class (+1 per four effective levels), and the Master's impossible stride (+20 feet of speed).

A killer whose blade still wants work. While the Cutthroat holds the reins she fights as a ROGUE: the first wound she lands each round runs deeper, dealing an extra 1d6 damage per three effective levels, and her eye for the opening sharpens (+2 initiative).

A tracker who follows prey into death itself. While the Hunter holds the reins she fights as a RANGER: martial weapons, a ranger's full attack progression, a growing eye for the kill (+1 attack per four effective levels), and the Hunter's tireless pace (+10 feet of speed).

A paladin who fell at the Worldwound's first opening and simply refused to stop guarding it. While the Knight holds the reins she fights as a paladin: heavy armor and shields, a paladin's full attack progression, climbing dodge and resistance bonuses to defense (+1 per four and per three effective levels), and immunity to shaken and frightened.

A druid of the old forests who poured herself into the roots rather than let her grove burn, and never fully died. While the Antlered One holds the reins a dire wolf appears beside the vessel and fights for as long as the spirit stays, fading the moment she withdraws. The vessel keeps the druid's Thorn Lash and Mend.
A whip of living thorns rakes a single target: 1d6 piercing damage per two shaman levels (maximum 10d6). Reflex halves.
Roots and sap knit torn flesh: heals the target 1d6 damage per two shaman levels (maximum 10d6).

A sorceress who chose to burn rather than surrender her city, and whose fire never went out. While the Pyre Empress holds the reins, the vessel wields her fire - the Cinder Bolt and the Pyre Burst - as often as she can bear to raise her hand.
A lance of the Empress's fire strikes a single target: 1d6 fire damage per two shaman levels (maximum 10d6). Reflex halves.
The fire that took her city, briefly relit: a 20-foot burst of flame dealing 1d6 fire damage per two shaman levels (maximum 10d6) to enemies in the area. Reflex halves.

A wizard who catalogued every death in the Worldwound, and read the ledger so often that the fears learned to read back. While the Pale Archivist holds the reins the vessel speaks her indices of dread. She teaches no wards and no blessings; the ledger holds only fears.
The Archivist reads a single target its own entry: Will save or become frightened for 2 rounds.
The ledger falls open and the page stares back: enemies within 30 feet must pass a Will save or be shaken for 2 rounds.

A duelist who fused sword and spell so thoroughly that neither survived her apart. While the Spellblade holds the reins, the vessel fights with the magus's weapon arts, and every weapon strike carries her parting fire: +1d6 fire damage per five effective levels.

The spell warrior uses his arcane knowledge rather than his rage to turn the tide of battle in favor of himself and his allies. With a clash of bracers and a sonorous chant, his song reaches out to touch the weapons of his allies, lending them arcane power. While his song does not inspire rage, he can use the power of his music to enchant the weapons of his allies. (The counterspelling arts of the tabletop warrior have no place in the Worldwound's wars - this port carries the weapon song only.)

While this raging song plays, the weapons of all allies within 60 feet gain an enhancement bonus: +1 at 1st level, increasing by 1 at 5th and every 5 levels thereafter to a maximum of +5 at 20th. The bonus overlaps rather than stacks with any enhancement a weapon already has. The song drains raging-song rounds for every round it plays.
The spell warrior's song flows through allied steel: weapons wielded by allies within 60 feet are enchanted while the song plays.
The crescendo skald's song inspires momentum rather than rage. Allies build speed as they keep landing blows and spells, and lose it after a quiet round. Spellcasting is never interrupted.

A raging song of momentum. While it plays, every ally within 60 feet gains one Momentum stack per round in which they land at least one attack or complete at least one spell, to a maximum of 5; a round with nothing landed resets that ally's stacks alone. Momentum grants a morale bonus to Strength and Constitution (+1 at one stack, +2 at three, +3 at five) and +1 on Will saves, at a cost of 1 AC. The song drains one raging-song round per round.

The crescendo carries this ally: a morale bonus to Strength and Constitution (+1 at one stack of Momentum, +2 at three, +3 at five) and +1 on Will saves, at a cost of 1 AC while it lasts. Each round with at least one landed attack or completed spell adds a stack, to a maximum of 5; a round with nothing landed resets it.

The dreadnaught hunts the mind instead of the blind side. She wears heavy armor without spoiling her study, and the mark she lays drains a foe's courage and saving throws. This replaces sneak attack and one slayer talent.

A swift-action study that marks a foe: a penalty on all of its saving throws (-1 at 1st level, increasing by 1 at 5th and every 5 levels thereafter, to -5 at 20th) for 10 minutes. There is no attack or damage bonus. A fresh mark also attempts to demoralize, a Persuasion check against 10 + its level + its Wisdom; on a success it is shaken for 1 minute. She adds half her level on Persuasion checks and is proficient with heavy armor.
The Dreadnaught's mark: a penalty on all three saving throws while it lasts. The deeper her study, the deeper the dread.
The Dreadnaught's Will is not the slayer's weak one, but stands halfway to a champion's: +1 at 1st level, +2 at 8th, +3 at 15th.

While paladins and inquisitors use their connection with the divine to fight undead hordes and other horrors of the night, a grave warden relies on knowledge, skill with weapons, and tenacity to put an end to these night-born terrors. His blade carries holy water's bite, he wards himself against death itself, and the oldest undead fear his finishing stroke: one that does not merely slay them, but unmakes them.

As a swift action, the grave warden anoints his held weapon for 1 round. While the anointment lasts, his weapon damage against undead creatures carries an additional 2d6 points of holy damage, as if from a direct hit by holy water.
As a standard action, the grave warden performs the warding rites upon himself, gaining the benefits of death ward for 1 minute per slayer level.

As a swift action he marks a single undead creature for 1 round. If his next attack against it hits, the target must succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + half his slayer level + Intelligence modifier) or be destroyed outright. A target that saves is immune to this grave warden's dustbringer for 24 hours.
The grave warden's killing stroke waits upon the next blow that lands. When it does, the undead must save or be unmade.
This creature has withstood the grave warden's dustbringer within the last day and cannot be marked again yet.

An eldritch scrapper blends weapons with spells. She trains with every weapon a soldier might carry, and her battlefield instincts let her pick up combat tricks her caster studies never left time for. (Tabletop port: the conflicting blood of the tabletop's trades is paid in spells known instead - one fewer at every level, the same price the crossblooded pays.)

The overchanneler opens her blood's channel wider than her body was meant to bear. While it is open her spells strike harder, last longer, and count for more, but each casting burns her as it leaves. This replaces one spell slot of every level per day.

As a swift action she opens the channel for 1 round. While it is open her caster level increases (+2 at 1st, +4 at 9th, +6 at 17th) and her spells carry that much bonus damage. The moment a spell leaves her through the open channel she takes damage equal to 3 per level of the spell cast.
The channel is open: her caster level is increased and her spells carry bonus damage equal to that increase - and her blood burns for 3 damage per spell level as each spell leaves.
The channel is opened to its apex: +8 caster level and +8 bonus damage on her spells, with no blood price. This peak can be reached once per day.
The overchanneler's veins have learned to close around the burn: her backlash damage can no longer reduce her below 1 hit point.
Once per day, the overchanneler may open the channel to its apex: +8 caster level and +8 damage per spell level for one round, with no backlash at all.

Unlike many warpriests, sacred fists leave behind armor and shield and instead rely on their fists and whatever protection their deity bestows on them. Their deity guards them as they fight unarmored, their strikes fall like a monk's in a flurry of blows, and their style - adopted in the monasteries of their faith - completes the art.

The sacred fist's deity shields his body: he gains a +2 sacred bonus on Fortitude saving throws. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's avoid-the-effect-entirely rule is not something the game exposes to mods; a save bonus stands in its place.)
The mending blade's god answers through steel rather than a holy symbol. Every wound he inflicts heals the allies fighting beside him. This replaces channel energy.

Whenever he damages an enemy, every living ally within 30 feet, himself included, is healed for a share of the damage dealt as positive energy, rounded down, minimum 1. The share reaches 10% at 8th level, and from 16th level the first hit of each round surges to 15% (the first two hits at 20th level). The radius grows to 45 feet at 10th level and 60 feet at 20th. Weapon damage, spells, and lingering damage all count; damage dealt to allies pays nothing.

His blessed tithe becomes negative energy. Undead allies are healed by it exactly as before, but living allies are scorched instead, though never below 1 hit point. Requires: Blessed Tithe (the Mending Blade archetype).

The undead master commands the dead rather than studying them. He fills his book with the animate line, and at the end of his studies the dead accept him as one of their own. This replaces the wizard bonus feats at 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level. (Tabletop port: the Horror Adventures archetype with documented adaptations.)

The undead master casts the Command Undead spell as a special ability, on its own pool: 3 uses per day, plus one at 6th, 12th, and 18th level. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's Command Undead feat, powered by channel energy or school-power uses, does not exist in this game - the real spell stands in for it.)

His studies fill his spellbook with the animate line: lesser animate dead at 3rd level, animate dead at 5th, and undeath to death at 11th. (Tabletop port: the tabletop also grants repair undead, undead anatomy, create undead, create greater undead, and cursed earth, none of which exist on this game's spell list, and allows spontaneous casting of the whole list, which the engine does not expose.)

The inkbound wizard has made a covenant with a living grimoire. He begins each battle with a blank book and writes spells into it as he casts, growing stronger the longer the fight lasts. This replaces arcane bond and the wizard bonus feats at 10th, 15th, and 20th level.

Each wizard spell he casts in combat leaves one measure of ink in the book. The well holds 10 measures at 1st level and 2 more for every five wizard levels after that, and the book starts each session blank. Ink is spent on quillwork: Blot (1 ink) and Wordwall (2 ink) are available immediately, Recitation from 5th level. Quillwork cannot be used without enough ink, and the ink does not persist through save and load.
Cost: 1 ink. A stain across the target's destiny: -2 on attack rolls, saving throws, and AC for 1 round (swift action). With Iron-Gall Ink the stain darkens to -3.
A stain across destiny: penalties on attacks, saves, and AC.
Cost: 2 ink. A wall of script rises before an ally: +4 deflection bonus to AC for 1 round (swift action). With Iron-Gall Ink the wall thickens to +6.
A wall of script: a deflection bonus to AC.

Cost: 3 ink. The book screams a stolen syllable at one enemy, dealing sonic damage equal to 5 plus twice the Inkbound's wizard level (standard action). From 11th level the scream carries a stain with it: the target also takes the Blot, at no further cost in ink.
The ink darkens with use: Blot's penalties worsen to -3, and Wordwall's wall thickens to +6.
The book writes ON him: the Inkbound gains a +2 natural armor bonus to AC, always.
Once per day, as a swift action, the book finishes itself: the ink floods back to full.

He animates a corpse companion from the lich's own legion and commands it in battle, choosing a shield-bearing tank, a two-handed brute, an archer, or a dual wielder. The corpse is player-controlled, grows with him, and occupies the standard companion slot - so an undead master who takes the Lich path commands both this and the path's skeletal champion. This replaces arcane bond; he cannot gain a familiar. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's corpse companion, realized with the lich mythic path's own undead pets.)
Animate a shield-bearing bulwark that holds the line from the lich's legion. It is player-controlled and levels with the undead master.
Animate a brute with a great blade for crushing blows from the lich's legion. It is player-controlled and levels with the undead master.
Animate a skeletal archer raining bone-fletched arrows from the lich's legion. It is player-controlled and levels with the undead master.
Animate a whirling storm of twin blades from the lich's legion. It is player-controlled and levels with the undead master.

Rather than drawing power from bestial aspects, the elementalist shifter channels power from the Inner Sphere - the planes of Air, Earth, Fire, and Water. She charges her strikes with elemental force and steps into a living elemental body. Trades her shifter aspects (and their wild shapes), her claws, and her chimeric aspects. (Tabletop port: the Ultimate Wilderness archetype with documented adaptations.)

Choose an elemental aspect: Air, Earth, Fire, or Water. Each grants its minor form as an always-on passive and its Elemental Strike. A second aspect is gained at 5th level, a third at 10th, and the fourth at 15th.
The minor form of Air: the storm's caress: +2 Dexterity (growing to +4 at 8th and +6 at 15th level); her strike crackles with electricity.
The minor form of Earth: the mountain's patience: +2 Constitution (growing to +4 at 8th and +6 at 15th level); her strike weeps acid.
The minor form of Fire: the flame's hunger: +2 Dexterity (growing to +4 at 8th and +6 at 15th level); her strike burns.
The minor form of Water: the wave's crush: +2 Strength (growing to +4 at 8th and +6 at 15th level); her strike freezes.

As a swift action, charge her melee attacks with elemental energy for 1 round: they deal an additional 1d6 energy damage of her chosen element, increasing by 1d6 every 4 levels to a maximum of 6d6 at 20th. Only one strike can be active at a time, and only elements chosen with elemental aspect can be used. This replaces shifter claws.
At 4th level, the elementalist shifter can assume the form of a Medium elemental of any element she has chosen, as elemental body I, at will (standard action). This replaces wild shape.

At 9th level she can fuse two of her elemental aspects, manifesting their combined power as a natural phenomenon. She learns one fusion of her choosing, and a second at 15th level; each requires its two aspects. Entering one is a swift action lasting 1 minute, usable at will. (Tabletop port of the tabletop ability, which fuses minor forms passively.)
Air and fire swirl into a storm of ash around her: ranged attacks against her suffer a 20% miss chance. (Air + Fire.) Entering the fusion is a swift action and it lasts 1 minute.

Air and water combine into torrential rain: she is soaked and fireproof, gaining fire resistance 10. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's fire-extinguishing rain. Air + Water.) Entering the fusion is a swift action and it lasts 1 minute.

Earth and water churn into a moving aura of mud: she gains a +4 bonus to her combat maneuver defense. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's difficult-terrain aura. Earth + Water.) Entering the fusion is a swift action and it lasts 1 minute.

Air and earth combine into a howling sandstorm: each round, enemies within 20 feet of her take 1d6 points of damage. (The tabletop's nonlethal damage and light-dimming are simplified. Air + Earth.) Entering the fusion is a swift action and it lasts 1 minute.

Fire and water explode into a cloud of steam: she gains 20% concealment against all attacks. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's obscuring-mist cloud. Fire + Water.) Entering the fusion is a swift action and it lasts 1 minute.

Earth and fire fuse beneath her feet: her melee attacks deal an additional 1d6 points of fire damage. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's burning-ground terrain. Earth + Fire.) Entering the fusion is a swift action and it lasts 1 minute.

The beastbound shifter's animal companion wears the aspects she would have taken herself, becoming a player-controlled beast drawn from the game's own menagerie. This replaces her aspects, claws, and chimeric aspects; she keeps defensive instinct and her wild skills.

Choose a linked aspect for her companion: the real shifter aspect is granted to the beast itself - its minor form is always on, and its major form appears on the companion's own ability bar, ready for the beast to shift into. She gains another link at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

Links this aspect to her companion. The beast receives the real shifter aspect: the minor-form passive is always on, and its major form, the real wild shape, sits on the beast's own ability bar. While linked the beast also gains a morale bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage that grows with her shifter level: +2, then +3 at 8th, +4 at 15th. The shifter does not shift; the beast does.

Paragons of battle, eschewing sermons for steel - living conduits of divine power, down to their very blood, which they happily shed in a moment if it brings greater glory to their deity. A 10-level prestige class (d10, full base attack) for those who already channel energy: bleeding stigmata, a shield of faith, and divine spellcasting that keeps growing. (Tabletop port of the Advanced Player's Guide prestige class.)

As a swift action, the vindicator wraps himself in his faith for 1 minute, gaining a +2 sacred bonus to AC. The shield strengthens as he does: +3 at 4th level, +4 at 7th, +5 at 10th. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's channel-fed 24-hour shield, scaled to class level.)

Two stances, each a swift action lasting 1 minute. Stigmata of Wrath grants a sacred bonus equal to half his class level, rounded up, on attack rolls and weapon damage; Stigmata of the Martyr grants the same bonus on saving throws and AC. While either is active he takes damage equal to half his class level every round. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's pick-one-of-five, condensed to offense and defense.)

Healing the vindicator casts on himself is buoyed by his faith: it gains a bonus equal to half his class level (round up). At 8th level the bonus doubles. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's empower-then-maximize, done as flat bonuses.)

While his stigmata bleed, the vindicator's blood runs down his weapons: his melee attacks deal an additional 1d6 points of damage. (Tabletop port: the tabletop's Channel Smite rider - Channel Smite itself does not exist in this game.)

At 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 10th level, the vindicator gains spells per day as if he had also gained a level in a divine spellcasting class he belonged to. Pick the same class each time (cleric, druid, inquisitor, or hunter). (Warpriest and oracle advancement does not exist in this engine - documented limitation.)

Every deathless legion needs an officer who does not flinch. The Bonewatch is the marshal of the dead - the one who stands in the gap between the living world and the ranks he commands, banner in hand, wearing the grave's own armor. A 5-level prestige class (d10, full base attack) for those sworn to the dead: bone armor, the command of graves, and an unbreakable last stand.
The grave grows on him: +2 natural armor to AC, thickening by another +2 at 4th level.
The marshal speaks and the dead obey: he casts the Command Undead spell as a special ability, 1 use per day (2 per day at 3rd level).
The marshal's will drives the dead onward: +2 on attack rolls and weapon damage.
The marshal's will drives his ranks: every pet he controls within 30 feet gains a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage. (The aura refreshes each round while he stands.)
Once per day, as a swift action, the marshal gives the order that cannot be disobeyed - not even by death: for 1 round, no damage can reduce him below 1 hit point.
The order stands: for 1 round, no damage can reduce the marshal below 1 hit point.

There is magic in her blood and she has never once asked it for anything. Where another bloodrager learns to shape the power that runs in her veins, the reckless bloodrager spends all of it on the swing - no spells, no subtlety, only the conviction that whatever is standing in front of her will be standing there a moment less than she will. She gives up blood casting entirely for the fury of a woman who has decided in advance that defence is somebody else's problem.

At 4th level the reckless bloodrager stops holding anything back. She gains a +2 bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls, and takes a -2 penalty to Armor Class. The bonus and the penalty are the same decision seen from two sides.

At 12th level the abandonment deepens: the bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls rises to +4 in total. The penalty to Armor Class does not worsen - by now she has learned exactly how much of herself to spend.

Some paladins are the sword. She is the wall. The sacred shield has given up the smite that her order is known for and taken up the older work instead: standing between what is behind her and what is coming. She does not destroy the wicked so much as refuse them, and after a while the refusal is its own kind of judgement.
At 3rd level the paladin's shield becomes the instrument of her oath rather than a piece of equipment. She gains a +2 shield bonus to Armor Class. This replaces smite evil.

She gains a +2 sacred bonus to Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saves, and damage reduction 5/evil: physical damage that is not evil-aligned is reduced by 5. Granted at 11th level, alongside the sacred shield's other defenses.

Someone in her line was bitten and lived, and the family has not been entirely human since. The bloodmarked sorcerer's power does not come only from her bloodline - it comes from the thing her bloodline came from. She has the bite whether she wants it or not, the hide that goes with it, and a serenity about violence that unsettles people who have never had to think about the moon.

The mark is in the blood and the blood shows. The bloodmarked sorcerer gains a bite natural attack, and a +2 bonus on Will saves - the weretouched are not easily turned, having been turned once already.

The priest of the Iron Creed holds that a warrior who needs his armor blessed has already lost the argument. He fights unarmored by choice and strikes considerably harder for it. This replaces sacred armor.
The whole of the blessing, poured into one edge. The priest of the Iron Creed gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls. This replaces sacred armor.
At 8th level the blessing deepens: the bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls rises to +3 in total. He has been saying the same prayer for eight years and it has stopped being a request.
At 14th level the bonus on attack rolls and weapon damage rolls rises to +4 in total, and the creed pays for itself in steel: he gains one bonus combat feat chosen from the fighter's list.

He did not find his magic. He was given it, by something that wanted something in return, and the terms were not negotiable. The pact wizard has no familiar and no bonded object - the thing he is bound to is not an item and does not live in a satchel. What the pact gives him is spells he did not learn and could not have chosen: they arrive on schedule, at the levels his patron decides, and they are always the same five.
A spell the patron wrote into his book. He did not research it, cannot replace it, and did not choose it. It is his regardless.

At 9th level the bloodmarked sorcerer stops resisting the shape her blood wants. She can take the form of a wolf, and the hide stays with her whether she changes or not - a +1 natural armor bonus to Armor Class. The change is not a spell and she does not lose herself in it; the wolf is family.

At 3rd level she can put herself where the blow is going to land. As a standard action she touches an ally and stands for them for 1 round: while the mark holds, all damage that would strike that ally strikes her instead, in full. There is no save and no splitting. She can lay the mark again as often as she has actions to lay it.
The sacred shield is standing for this creature. For one round, damage meant for them goes to her instead.
